raw_summary: A Tesla driver caught asleep behind the wheel on Ottawa’s Highway 417 during Tuesday’s rush hour now faces a careless driving charge from the Ontario Provincial Police. article_paragraphs: A Tesla driver caught asleep behind the wheel on Ottawa’s Highway 417 during Tuesday’s rush hour now faces a careless driving charge from the Ontario Provincial Police. The photo OPP shared shows a new-generation Model Y in traffic.

The charge carries a $490 fine and six demerit points on conviction. It’s at least the fifth time this year Canadian police have gone public with a sleeping Tesla driver, and it’s not a coincidence that it’s happening as “Full Self-Driving” gets better.

OPP East Region posted about the stop Wednesday morning. Police didn’t name the brand or the driver-assist system, but the message was clear: “even though your vehicle has an autonomous driving feature, drivers are still required to pay due care and attention when behind the wheel.”

According to OPP, the officer could see the driver’s eyes were closed and hands were off the steering wheel. Instead of lighting up the cruiser, police pulled in close to capture body camera footage first.
Ottawa is the latest, but British Columbia has been dealing with this all year:
This isn’t new in Canada either. Back in 2020, Alberta RCMP went further and criminally charged a Tesla driver caught sleeping on Autopilot at 150 km/h with dangerous driving.

The U.S. has the same problem with less enforcement. In September, Colorado State Patrol got a report of a sleeping Tesla driver on I-70 near Georgetown and never found the car. The same month, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi pressed the DOT after NBC News found 43 videos of drivers apparently asleep in moving Teslas , 17 of them posted in 2026 alone.
And in October, a driver told CHP he was asleep on FSD when his Tesla drove into a closed crash scene and hit a patrol car in Fairfield, California. Two officers were seriously injured.

raw_title: What's The Worst Way You've Abused A Rental Car?
title: What's The Worst Way You've Abused A Rental Car?
raw_summary: Unless you only travel within driving distance of home or are willing to spend the time and money on shipping , we will all end up in a situation where renting a car is a necessity. There may be plenty of cities with fantastic public transportation systems, but you just need a car to venture out and explore the countryside. Many of us are far more care-free behind the wheel when the vehicle is owned by an abstract corporate entity and not a person with a face. What's the worst way you've abused a rental car? I'm not talking about returning it with an empty tank. That's just a surcharge that rental companies are more than happy to add to your bill. Abuse is real, lasting damage that's an absolute nightmare to reverse. Let me use a hypothetical beach day in the South of France as an example. You and a few friends take a decent Peugeot 408 to a sleepy village on the Mediterranean. After a fun day of sand and surf, everyone piles back into the sedan right off the beach, covering the interior with sand. That's the appetizer. On the drive back, you get impatient sitting behind a truck on a two-lane road. You pull into the oncoming lane but don't get entirely clear, and you sideswipe the truck. The 408 is far worse off, with its entire right side scratched up. That's abuse!

Besides outright crashing a rental car, the worst thing you could do is race a pack of them. Rental car racing actually is a significant part of NASCAR lore. The mischievous tradition has endured stock car racing's evolution from a moonshiners' pastime to a billion-dollar sport. Several current Cup Series drivers have admitted to racing each other and their team members. In many instances, rental car racing is just a fun way to salvage a rained-out test day. Everyone just piles on to the track once the showers stop and run laps to dry the racing surface. On race day, it's pushing the limit on the drive out of the track. Joe Gibbs Racing driver Chase Briscoe told The Athletic in 2025, "Honestly, the craziest thing, I think, is watching the team guys leave a racetrack. It is like the best racing and just the most chaos you've ever seen in your life."

The new fifth generation of Honda’s two-motor hybrid system will once again pair with an Atkinson-cycle four-cylinder gas engine. title: 2028 Honda CR-V Will Go Hybrid-Only, Following The Toyota RAV4's Lead
raw_summary: We've been living with affordable hybrid vehicles for almost three decades now, but it's taken a surprisingly long time for some of the best-selling cars in the U.S. to go hybrid-only, even for models that have offered reliable hybrids for years. Toyota started doing it with the current Camry and new RAV4 , and now Honda has confirmed that the next-gen CR-V will only be sold with hybrid powertrains. Honda says the seventh-generation CR-V will be revealed next year, in time for the SUV's 30th anniversary, and it will ride on a new platform and use the company's new two-motor hybrid system, which our own Andy Kalmowitz got to try out in a Civic prototype last year. This new powertrain is said to be more powerful and more efficient, and the modular architecture is more rigid while being lighter-weight. It should be cheaper for Honda to produce, too, and a new electric all-wheel-drive system will be a big improvement.

article_paragraphs: We've been living with affordable hybrid vehicles for almost three decades now, but it's taken a surprisingly long time for some of the best-selling cars in the U.S. to go hybrid-only, even for models that have offered reliable hybrids for years. Toyota started doing it with the current Camry and new RAV4 , and now Honda has confirmed that the next-gen CR-V will only be sold with hybrid powertrains.

Honda says the seventh-generation CR-V will be revealed next year, in time for the SUV's 30th anniversary, and it will ride on a new platform and use the company's new two-motor hybrid system, which our own Andy Kalmowitz got to try out in a Civic prototype last year. This new powertrain is said to be more powerful and more efficient, and the modular architecture is more rigid while being lighter-weight. It should be cheaper for Honda to produce, too, and a new electric all-wheel-drive system will be a big improvement.

Somehow we didn't get a hybrid CR-V in the U.S. until the 2020 model year, when the fifth-gen model was facelifted. Since then, annual CR-V hybrid sales have grown almost tenfold, and it currently makes up more than 50% of total CR-V sales. With the price difference between the hybrid and the regular CR-V being so relatively minor, and the gains in driving experience being so large, it makes sense to just hybridize the entire lineup. This year will be the third straight year in which Honda sells more than 400,000 CR-Vs , and upping the average efficiency of that many cars can make a big difference .

Many U.S.-spec CR-Vs are currently built in Ohio (the rest being made in Indiana), and Honda just announced plans for a new $3 billion plant in Ohio that will focus on hybrids , though gas-only and fully electric cars will be built there as well. Production there won't start until 2029, but Honda envisions an annual capacity of 240,000 units. Honda says it will introduced 15 new hybrids by 2030, most of which will be oriented towards the American market.

One of those hybrids will be the model at the top of this slide, or at least something similar to it. That rakish fastback is officially called the Hybrid Sedan Prototype , and it's probably just the next-gen Accord that's due to come out in the very near future. It wears what will be Honda's new design language, and you don't have to imagine how it'll look on the CR-V — lightly camouflaged prototypes have already been spied, as you can see from the Instagram post below.

I think it's looking pretty good, though it's a shame that the CR-V will seemingly lose its signature vertical taillights . We probably won't have to wait long to see the CR-V; expect an actual auto show debut, simply because a car this popular can actually take the spotlight and be of interest to the regular people who still go to shows. A Detroit Auto Show debut in January seems like a safe bet, but Honda could wait for Chicago in February or New York in March.

title: The most tradable sport nobody trades': Inside race prediction platform RPM
raw_summary: RPM is the world’s first motorsport prediction platform, where every outcome of a race event becomes a tradable market. Fans are able to buy and sell outcomes on every moment of a race at a moment’s notice. Founder Ben Jarrett joined The Race Business as part of our Spotlight series of interviews to explain how he spotted a niche in the motorsport market - and how RPM itself could play a part in changing how fans consume motorsport.

article_paragraphs: RPM is the world’s first motorsport prediction platform, where every outcome of a race event becomes a tradable market. Fans are able to buy and sell outcomes on every moment of a race at a moment’s notice.

Founder Ben Jarrett joined The Race Business as part of our Spotlight series of interviews to explain how he spotted a niche in the motorsport market - and how RPM itself could play a part in changing how fans consume motorsport.
“RPM is at the intersection of motorsport, content creation, and prediction markets,” says Jarrett.
Fans can essentially make predictions about every single facet of motorsport. And it’s an idea that was born out of a racetrack.
“I was racing GT4 cars, and I’m standing on the pitwall. Someone comes up and says: ‘10 bucks, he puts it into the wall at Turn 1’.
“The other guy’s like, ‘No, no, 100 bucks, he puts it [into the wall]’.
“Everyone was standing there. I was in my suit, I had my hands on my helmet, and we were supposed to go out there for practice before qualifying and put a lap in.”
It was at that moment that Jarrett had the idea to open up motorsport prediction markets to fans and content creators.

article_paragraphs: The South Delhi District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed Eicher Motors and Noida-based Shree Mahadev Motors to jointly pay Rs 1 lakh to a Royal Enfield Interceptor 650 owner. The order, dated 4 November 2026, concerns a September 2021 trip to Leh during which the rider said his motorcycle repeatedly lost power . The commission found no email on record showing that corrective work had been carried out on his bike.

The complainant, Hasan Murtaza, bought the Interceptor 650 from Ess Aar Motors on 13 April 2019. Before setting out for Leh, he took the motorcycle to Shree Mahadev Motors in June 2021. According to his complaint, he told the service centre about the planned trip and specifically asked it to update the electronic control unit (ECU) to address reports of power loss at high altitude. He said the workshop told him the update had been installed and the bike was ready for the trip.

Murtaza said the motorcycle lost power at around 15,912 feet and that he had to drag the roughly 200 kg bike downhill to restart it. The power loss continued on the way to Leh, where he arrived on 21 September 2021. He took the bike to an authorised Royal Enfield service centre the next day. According to his account, a representative there told him the ECU had never been updated and the workshop lacked the equipment to do it.

Murtaza said he left the motorcycle at a hotel in Leh because he was concerned about continuing the trip. He later returned to collect it and rode it back to Noida, where he said the same problem persisted on the return journey. After corresponding with customer support and sending a legal notice in January 2022, he filed a consumer complaint seeking Rs 1 crore for physical discomfort and mental distress .

The commission reviewed the purchase invoice, an article about the high-altitude ECU issue and the rider’s email correspondence. The opposing side argued that the record lacked job cards from the Noida and Leh workshops and that Eicher and its dealer dealt with each other as independent businesses. Shree Mahadev Motors did not appear or file a reply despite receiving notice.

The commission said the emails established which authorised service centre Murtaza visited in Leh and when he visited it. It found no contradiction in the documents relating to the trip and no email showing that corrective work had been done on the motorcycle. It also noted that the medical records showed breathlessness and wheezing on exertion, with no recorded asthma diagnosis.

The commission di rected Eicher Motors and Shree Mahadev Motors to pay Rs 1 lakh jointly and severally within three months of the order. If they miss that deadline, interest at 6% per annum will apply from the date of the order until payment. The commission named Ess Aar Motors as the selling dealer and directed the other two parties to pay the award.

Perhaps the polar opposite of a Mercedes of any era in build quality, safety, and engineering is the backyard-built kit car. Arising in the late 1950s and carrying through its heyday in the 1970s, home-built kit cars typically started with a donor chassis, often from an old Triumph or VW. A fresh fiberglass body gave that chassis new life, and the builder a sense of pride in creating a working, drivable car.

The Meyers Manx SR2 we looked at on Wednesday was an example—and an extremely rare one at that—of a '70s-era kit car. Created by industry legend Bruce Meyers, the SR2 proved to be his swan song, as his company folded shortly after its launch. That makes the small clutch of original SR2s (about 200 total) far more dear when they do come on the market. Our SR2 came with Corvair power and an interior ready for the next owner's taste in upholstery. At $17,000, however, that wasn't a winning combo. You all expected more for that amount and sent the Manx packing with a massive 93% 'No Dice' loss.

The closest today's 1995 Mercedes-Benz E320 Estate comes to a kit car is that it's the same model year Mercedes-Benz India, Ltd. began building similar models from knock-down kits at its Chakan assembly plant. This is also nearly the last year for the W124 series as a whole, as it was replaced, body style by body style, over the course of the next three years: 1995 (saloons), 1996 (estates), 1997 (coupes), and 1998 (cabriolets). Mercedes is nothing if not methodical.

This generation, which represents the facelifted version of the W124, was also the first to carry Mercedes' new naming convention of a class letter followed by a number indicating—sometimes only semi-accurately—engine displacement. The company has carried on this convention to this day. Because of that simple nomenclature, we can tell from the name that this is a mid-size E-Class (Executive class) model with a 3.2-liter engine. See? Easy-peasy.

That 3.2-liter engine is an M104.992 straight-six with double-overhead cams and four valves per cylinder. In North American guise, it produces a workmanlike 217 horsepower and 229 pound-feet of torque. As in all U.S.-bound cars, here it's matched with a five-speed 4G-Tronic automatic actuated through Mercedes' traditional pixelated snake shift gate.

According to the ad, this car has undergone significant repairs and maintenance over its 159,850 miles. The seller notes that under their ownership, they replaced the engine wiring harness, head and head gasket, radiator, and water pump. In addition, the car has a new climate control panel and has had two failed window regulators replaced. Other plusses include Continental tires with plenty of tread left and "flawlessly working" A/C.

With all that in the rearview, the seller now describes the car as "sorted and in excellent working condition." The receipts for the work will accompany the car in the sale for the next owner's reading enjoyment.

The Lamborghini Temerario was introduced in 2024, serving as a replacement for the V10-powered Huracan, albeit with a more potent plug-in-hybrid V8 setup. While the Temerario is sharper, more technologically advanced, and faster than its predecessor, its engine sound isn't as dramatic as some fans had hoped for.

In order to fix this issue and make its baby supercar more desirable, Lamborghini has unveiled an optional titanium exhaust system. This promises to "amplify the natural acoustic character" of the Temerario's twin-turbo V8 engine while being lighter than the standard unit. The system was developed in collaboration with Slovenian specialist Akrapovič, as a follow-up to earlier projects for the Urus and the Huracan.

The lightweight exhaust is part of the automaker's Accessori Originali catalog, but it will also be offered as a retrofit option for existing owners. Furthermore, Lamborghini has confirmed it will find its way onto the first Temerario derivative, which is scheduled to debut next week, likely adding a retractable top into the mix.

The hand-assembled Akrapovič exhaust is made of high-grade titanium alloys with precision-cast valve housings and a "dedicated" black finish for the tailpipe. According to Lamborghini, the system tips the scales at 25.1 pounds (11.4 kg), which is 12% lighter than the standard component.

More importantly, it benefits from a revised geometry with larger tubes, custom manifolds, a new silencer architecture, upgraded heat insulation, and retuned NVH settings. As a result, it produces deeper notes at low revs and an "incisive acoustic signature" as the V8 moves closer to the 10,000-rpm limiter .

The Lamborghini Temerario is powered by a twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 engine working together with a trio of electric motors and a 3.8-kWh lithium-ion battery pack. The plug-in-hybrid powertrain has a combined output of 907 horsepower (677 kW / 920 PS), which is much closer to the Revuelto than the discontinued Huracan was to the Aventador, or the older Gallardo to the Murcielago.

Just as noteworthy as the availability of the Akrapovič exhaust for the coupe is a line tucked into the end of Lamborghini's press release. It mentions a new derivative of the supercar, which is scheduled to premiere next week.

Even though Mahindra BE 6 and XEV 9e are manufactured here in India, they were conceived and designed back in England. At the M.A.D.E. headquarters in Banbury, Oxfordshire, UK, to be precise. Mahindra’s Formule e racing team is based out of UK too, if you were wondering.

2027 is fast approaching and Mahindra is taking greater strides towards increased global presence and the company’s eyes are on the UK market. Three Mahindra Electric Origin SUVs (two launched and one upcoming) are reportedly in the pipeline to make a grand debut in Britain, targeting upper end of mainstream market.

BE 6 and XEV 9e along with the upcoming BE 7 are the three vehicles that are planned to launch in the UK next year. Considering that the UK is also a right-hand-drive market like India, adapting India-spec BE 6, XEV 9e and BE 7 (when it is launched) should not pose great hurdles, except for a few market-specific norms like cybersecurity compliance requirements.

After UK, Mahindra is also eyeing the European market. Both India-UK FTA and India-EU FTA (Free Trade Agreement) are likely to work in Mahindra’s favour to establish a steady sales and after-sales supply line from India to UK and Europe.

As per the report, Mahindra BE 6, XEV 9e may launch some time in 2027 in the UK. The timeline can be pushed to 2028, depending on market-specific compliances and other hurdles. BE 7 launch is likely to happen following BE 6 and XEV 9e. The prospect of XEV 9S for UK and EU are slightly less as three row seating is not very popular.

Where pricing is concerned, the report mentioned a price tag of around GBP 41,000 for BE 6 (approx Rs 51 lakh), GBP 48,000 for XEV 9e (approx Rs 60 lakh) and GBP 52,000 for BE 7 (approx Rs 65 lakh). raw_summary: Canada’s government wants to make it easier for citizens to drive electric, and they’re putting more than $4 billion in funding for electricity infrastructure and grid modernization that includes more than 55,000 new EV chargers. The proposed federal budget set aside $4 billion (CAD) for grid improvements, with a $~635 million carveout specifically for EV charging infrastructure with $587 million of that set aside to renew the Zero-Emission Vehicle Infrastructure Program (ZEVIP), which funds the development of new public EV charging stations.

article_paragraphs: Canada’s government wants to make it easier for citizens to drive electric, and they’re putting more than $4 billion in funding for electricity infrastructure and grid modernization that includes more than 55,000 new EV chargers.

The proposed federal budget set aside $4 billion (CAD) for grid improvements, with a $~635 million carveout specifically for EV charging infrastructure with $587 million of that set aside to renew the Zero-Emission Vehicle Infrastructure Program (ZEVIP), which funds the development of new public EV charging stations.

“The charging industry is really encouraged by the multi-year investment in the budget,” explains Travis Allan, president and CEO of the Canadian Charging Infrastructure Council (CCIC) told Electric Autonomy . “We’ll be looking to make sure that we have great programs in place to deal with the barriers faced by people living in condos and apartments, public fast charging, which needs to cover major corridors and metropolitan areas, and then also charging for fleets and medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, which make up a major share of transportation emissions.”

The rest of the $4 billion will be spent on electricity infrastructure expansion over the next 10 years, starting in 2027 and running through 2036. Because it’s Canada where nearly 60% of electrical generation already comes from renewable hydro and wind power, renewable energy is a de-facto priority , with carveouts for the Smart Renewables and Electrification Pathways Program, new data and modeling efforts to guide grid planning, and $1.6 billion to modernize power systems in northern and remote communities.

The charging infrastructure program highlighted here, ZEVIP, would help charge point operators by covering up to 50% of eligible project expenses for most projects, and up to 75% of projects led by indigenous developers with caps of up to $2 million per project.

Canada continues to take steps to separate itself from the wild swings and economic chaos caused by America’s random tariffs, trade policies , and dumb oil wars – and building out an infrastructure that makes it easier for its citizens to give affordable Chinese EVs a chance while strengthening its relationship with the US’ biggest economic rival ?

If Washington doesn’t see that for, “Go pound sand, eh?” that it is, then it’s truly lost the plot – but even if the “blue wave” last week was enough to shake a little sense into the folks running the show, it may already be too late to patch things up.

We first covered the Honda UC3 earlier this year when the company announced plans to launch the electric scooter in Thailand and Vietnam. Designed as an electric equivalent to a 110cc gasoline-powered scooter, the UC3 is built for practical everyday transportation rather than weekend joyrides.

But don’t let its modest appearance fool you. The UC3 packs a 6 kW (8 hp) electric motor capable of reaching approximately 50 mph (80 km/h), making it more than capable of handling typical urban commuting.

Its 3.2 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery provides up to 76 miles (122 km) of range under WMTC testing. Unlike Honda’s other electric scooters that use removable batteries, the UC3 has a permanently installed battery that charges directly on the bike.
There’s also a full-color TFT display, smartphone connectivity, three riding modes, reverse gear, and a generous 26-liter under-seat storage compartment.
And perhaps most importantly, it comes from Honda, a company with decades of experience building reliable, affordable motorcycles.

The UC3 originally launched in Vietnam with prices starting around 78.5 million Vietnamese dong, or roughly $3,000. However, recent reports from Vietnamese dealerships show incentives bringing prices down to around 54 million dong, equivalent to approximately $2,100.
That’s a pretty compelling price for a 50 mph (80 km/h) electric scooter from one of the world’s largest motorcycle manufacturers.

It features a “four stage path to the top” and will start in December with an open-access format inviting every eligible driver to Silverstone, where 80 will be selected for stage two.
That will see the 80 drivers compete in the “GR63 Shootout” on 31 January to determine the 25 slots for an eight-round championship at Silverstone from March to November in 2027.
The championship is fully-funded for each driver and the top five will go head-to-head in stage four next December, where the winner will receive a fully-funded karting campaign in 2028.
“Karting is where it all started for me,” said Russell, who won titles on a national and international level before progressing into single-seater competition.
“It taught me everything I’ve relied on throughout my career. I know how hard it is for talented young drivers to get that first opportunity, especially when budgets are tight.
“With the GR63 Karting Academy, I want to give something back by finding those hidden talents and giving them the support and platform they need to reach their potential.

article_paragraphs: Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell has launched a new karting academy at Silverstone aimed at developing the next generation of motorsport talent, with 25 young drivers set to receive a fully funded championship opportunity in 2027.

The GR63 Karting Academy will be open to boys and girls aged eight and nine, with Russell hoping to provide a route into motorsport for talented youngsters who might otherwise be held back by the financial demands of the sport.
Based at Silverstone's karting circuit, the initiative will run across four stages, beginning with open-access qualifying sessions in December 2026.
The first stage will see eligible drivers compete in arrive-and-drive sessions between December 6 and 31, with the 80 fastest progressing to a shootout on January 31, 2027.

From there, 25 drivers will be selected for the GR63 Championship, an eight-round series running from March to November 2027. Each round will take place on a different circuit configuration at Silverstone, with all participation costs covered by the academy.
The 25 selected drivers will also receive a full set of academy equipment, including racing overalls, a helmet, gloves and boots.

The programme will culminate in December 2027, when the championship's top five finishers compete in a final race at Silverstone. Drivers will be evaluated on their talent, lap times, fitness, racecraft and media skills, with the overall winner receiving a fully-funded karting season in 2028.

article_paragraphs: Brazil’s take on the Grande Panda gets subtle styling tweaks and engines of its own.

The Fiat Grande Panda is a budget-friendly hatchback with crossover styling cues sold in Europe since 2024. Now, the model has a South American twin brother with a new name, symmetrical emblems, smoother doors, and a few changes under the hood.

Following spy shots of heavily camouflaged prototypes and shadowy teasers , Fiat has shared new official photos of the Argo X ahead of its market launch in Brazil in the coming months. At first glance, the new model looks like a spitting image of the Grande Panda, but a closer inspection reveals subtle market-specific styling revisions.

First of all, the doors have smoother panels, doing without the embossed Panda lettering stamped on the doors of the European model. Furthermore, the Fiat emblems on the grille and the tailgate adopt a symmetrical layout instead of the retro-inspired off-center placement, and there is an Argo X badge at the back. Finally, the South American model rides on a different set of diamond-cut alloy wheels and features a bi-tone livery with a black roof and pillars.
The rest of the design is common between the Argo X and the Grande Panda, including the boxy proportions, the raised stance, the plastic cladding with Fiat Easter Eggs, and the pixel-style LEDs.

Fiat has yet to release photos of the interior, which is expected to be slightly toned down compared to the Grande Panda. We also don't know the specifications, but local media have largely figured out what lies under the skin of the Argo X. The hatchback is underpinned by Stellantis' Smart Car architecture, which is shared with the Citroën C3 .

The big difference with the Grande Panda is expected to be the powertrain lineup. Instead of the turbocharged 1.2-liter three-cylinder engines of the European model, the South American twin is expected to be powered by 1.0-liter three-cylinder units running on both gasoline and ethanol. The entry-level naturally aspirated mill is expected to produce up to 74 horsepower (55 kW / 75 PS), paired to a five-speed manual gearbox. There might also be a turbocharged 1.0-liter engine with a 12-volt mild-hybrid system and an output of 114 hp (85 kW / 116 PS), combined with a CVT.
The Fiat Argo X will be manufactured at the Stellantis Automotive Hub in Betim, Brazil. The aging Argo hatchback will remain on sale, serving as a cheaper alternative to the newcomer.

article_paragraphs: Kia India has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Andhra Pradesh government to establish its second manufacturing plant in Anantapur. The project involves a combined investment of USD 2 billion by Kia and its supplier partners, with production planned to begin in early 2030. The new plant will have an installed capacity of 2 lakh vehicles a year, taking Kia’s total annual manufacturing capacity in India to 6.30 lakh units .

The proposed facility and its supplier operations will cover a combined 465 acres. Kia expects the project to generate around 12,000 direct and indirect jobs . The new plant will carry out stamping, welding, painting and assembly, the same four manufacturing processes handled at Kia’s existing Anantapur facility.

Kia lists its current plant’s annual capacity at 4.30 lakh units. The additional 2 lakh units represent an increase of around 47%. The existing site covers 945 acres, including supplier operations, and supports 24,237 direct and indirect jobs, according to Kia. The company puts the initial investment by Kia and its suppliers at the first site at USD 2.9 billion, with cumulative investment across the two plants expected to reach up to USD 5 billion (Rs 47,000 crores).

Kia says the second facility will manufacture new models across internal combustion and electric powertrains. The company has yet to name the models it will build there. Its existing plant produces the Seltos, Sonet, Syros, Carens, Carens Clavis, Carnival and Sorento. Kia’s current production mix in Anantapur already includes the Syros EV and Carens Clavis EV, CNG versions of the Carens and Carens Clavis, and the Sorento Hybrid.

Gwanggu Lee, Managing Director and CEO of Kia India , said the second plant would give the company more flexibility to respond to demand and introduce new models. He added that the expanded manufacturing base would serve both Indian and overseas markets.

Kia’s previously announced India roadmap targets annual sales of around 4.10 lakh units and a 7.6% market share by 2030. It also calls for eight electrified models, including hybrids and battery EVs, by the end of the decade. The Seltos Hybrid is expected in 2027, with hybrid versions of the Sonet and Carens planned by 2029. Kia has also outlined plans for another locally produced small electric SUV by 2029.
Those product timelines precede the second plant’s planned start of production in early 2030. Kia’s latest announcement leaves the allocation of those models across the two facilities open.

The Anantapur expansion follows Hyundai Motor Group’s October announcement of a USD 15.5 billion India investment programme for 2026–2032. That broader programme covers manufacturing, research and development, and supplier localisation. Kia’s latest MoU puts a location, production timeline and capacity figure on its own next phase of manufacturing expansion in India.

Creta, including the Creta Electric, led Hyundai’s lineup with 17,955 units. Sales were down 2.32% from 18,381 units in October 2025 but up 1.69% from 17,657 units in September 2026. Creta accounted for 28.59% of Hyundai’s October sales and finished 4,938 units ahead of Venue.

Venue’s record tally of 13,017 units was up 10.90% from 11,738 units a year earlier and 13.53% from 11,466 units in September. It added 1,551 units over the previous month, the biggest gain among Hyundai models with September sales. Creta and Venue together sold 30,972 units, accounting for just over 49% of Hyundai’s October volumes.

Exter took third place with 8,509 units, up 35.19% from 6,294 units a year earlier and 1.98% from 8,344 units in September. Its year-on-year gain of 2,215 units was the largest among Hyundai models with sales in October 2025. Aura finished fourth with 7,349 units. The compact sedan gained 26.38% YoY from 5,815 units, although sales slipped 2.40% from 7,530 units in September.

The i20 ranked fifth with 5,528 units, up 37.41% YoY and 1.88% MoM. It recorded the highest year-on-year percentage growth in Hyundai’s lineup, adding 1,505 units over October 2025. Grand i10 Nios finished just 70 units behind with 5,458 units. Its sales rose 0.59% from 5,426 units a year earlier and 4.36% from 5,230 units in September.

The newly launched Bayon entered the chart in seventh place with 3,449 units, giving it a 5.49% share of Hyundai’s October sales. Its first month on the chart accounted for more than 61% of the company’s month-on-month volume gain. Together with Creta, Hyundai as recorded 21,404 mid-size SUV sales in Oct. Hyundai aims to sell 2.5 lakh mid-size SUVs .

Verna took eighth place with 775 units, down 5.95% from 824 units a year earlier and up 1.71% from 762 units in September. Alcazar followed just 17 units behind at 758 units. The three-row SUV grew 2.16% MoM from 742 units, while sales fell 39.79% YoY from 1,259 units.

Hyundai sold one Ioniq 5 in October, compared with six units a year earlier and nine in September. Tucson is no longer on sale in India. With Bayon joining the lineup, Hyundai had six models above 5,000 units and seven above 3,000 units in October.

title: The High-Rise Bottleneck: Why EV Charging in Indian Apartments Is an Engineering Puzzle
raw_summary: Most Western clean-energy reporting takes a very specific picture of home charging for granted. You pull into a private driveway, plug into an attached garage wall-box, and pull cheap power while you sleep. Data from Kazam and the Alliance for an Energy Efficient Economy (AEEE) shows that roughly 70% to 75% of urban households in major Indian metros live in multi-family apartments and cooperative housing societies. It’s their own building.

Data from Kazam and the Alliance for an Energy Efficient Economy (AEEE) shows that roughly 70% to 75% of urban households in major Indian metros live in multi-family apartments and cooperative housing societies.
article_paragraphs: Most Western clean-energy reporting takes a very specific picture of home charging for granted. You pull into a private driveway, plug into an attached garage wall-box, and pull cheap power while you sleep.

Data from Kazam and the Alliance for an Energy Efficient Economy (AEEE) shows that roughly 70% to 75% of urban households in major Indian metros live in multi-family apartments and cooperative housing societies. Parking means an open ground level slot or a space two levels down in a concrete basement. When someone here buys an electric car, their biggest hurdle isn’t battery degradation or highway chargers. It’s their own building.

As an electrical engineer in India, I watch this play out every week. Someone buys an EV, assumes they can hire a local wireman to pull power from their flat’s meter to their parking bay, and runs straight into transformer limits, cable physics, and nervous managing committees.

Indian housing societies buy electricity under a bulk “sanctioned load” from their local utility (DISCOM). The utility sizes the local transformer using an electrical diversity factor the simple assumption that not all 100 flats will run their air conditioners, geysers, and induction stoves at the exact same moment.

A domestic geyser pulls 2 kW for ten minutes and shuts off. A 7.4 kW AC wall-box pulls 32 amps continuously for six to eight hours. When several residents plug in around 8:00 PM, that heavy, unbroken draw lands on the transformer right as domestic air conditioning and kitchen loads hit their evening peak.
Let’s look at the numbers on a 100-flat complex running on a standard 250 kVA transformer:

Here is where the grid cracks: just five or six cars charging at 7.4 kW pull 37 kW to 44 kW. That wipes out the 30 kW buffer completely. If eight cars plug in at once (59.2 kW), the transformer goes straight into thermal overload.

When that happens, the main incomer breaker trips plunging common areas and elevators into darkness or the utility slaps the society with massive Maximum Demand penalties on their next power bill. Getting a utility to upgrade a transformer or approve higher sanctioned load requires significant capital, transformer yard space, and months of red tape.

You pull into a private driveway, plug into an attached garage wall-box, and pull cheap power while you sleep.

raw_summary: Today is Veterans Day in the United States. Naturally, across the country, people have spent at least part of the day thinking about veterans they know as well as veterans they don’t and thanking them for their service. Whether you agree with the various wars the United States has gotten into or not, you have to honor and appreciate the human beings who offered to put their lives on the line in order to support their country (or think that they’re doing so, at least). I know several people who are veterans, and they typically sacrificed a lot in their previous military roles. However, I do have to come back to the rationale for the wars we as a country get into. We get into a war in the Middle East connected to XYZ, but it’s really about oil. After years of over-involvement, destruction, and death, society realizes it’s been a super counterproductive, idiotic war and we pull out. The, after a few years, we begin again and the story repeats.

Gaining control of the Senate and the House of Representatives has emboldened the Democrats, giving them a renewed sense of political legitimacy and a mandate to pursue their agenda. But will this shift translate into meaningful changes in US climate change policy?

The Democratic sweep will change the political dynamics around US climate policy and how the country cooperates with the international community on this issue. Although there was no official US presence at the 2025 COP conference, held in Brazil, a coalition of 100 local US leaders , including governors, mayors and other top city and state officials, attended as part of the US Climate Alliance. Former US vice-president Al Gore , and former US secretary of state John Kerry are part of an unofficial US group at the 2026 gathering.
Kerry said in a speech there : “Americans are committed to taking back their future, and we will build and rebuild our partnerships as we do that.”

Being on the ground at COP is important. As the US has a decisive role to play in global climate policy, sending a non-official coalition signals that many Americans are still working to combat climate change.

Trump has repeatedly stated that climate change is a hoax and refused to attend the COP31 climate talks being held in Turkey. But 20 Democratic members of Congress will be attending, although they have been denied official state department funding for the trip.

During the first and second Trump administrations, the US has been an outlier among wealthy countries when it comes to fighting climate change. Trump has actively backed the use of fossil fuels, undermining clean energy projects, and rolled back legislation that stipulated emission standards for vehicles .

Trump also weakened greenhouse gas reporting requirements and methane regulation . Then in February 2026, the Trump administration rescinded the Environmental Protection Agency’s 2009 finding that greenhouse gases threaten the health and welfare of the public, which had regulated the emissions from new cars and other vehicles. This had provided the legal foundation for regulation under the Clean Air Act .

title: 300 Glaciers Have Disappeared from the American West Since the Mid‑20th Century
raw_summary: From an airplane, most of the glaciers of the Rocky Mountain West look like small patches of white nestled into rugged landscape where the topography folds. The white is the snow cover, and lower down you can see the gray-blue bare ice. In the middle of the 20th century, over 1,450 glaciers could be found in the contiguous U.S. Together, they covered 217 square miles (562 square kilometers) in six western states. The white is the snow cover, and lower down you can see the gray-blue bare ice. In the middle of the 20th century, over 1,450 glaciers could be found in the contiguous U.S.
article_paragraphs: From an airplane, most of the glaciers of the Rocky Mountain West look like small patches of white nestled into rugged landscape where the topography folds. The white is the snow cover, and lower down you can see the gray-blue bare ice.

In the middle of the 20th century, over 1,450 glaciers could be found in the contiguous U.S. Together, they covered 217 square miles (562 square kilometers) in six western states. Today, a comprehensive review my colleagues and I just published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences shows their total area has shrunk by 35% and they are still shrinking, perhaps faster.
A little more than 300 glaciers have disappeared , way more than I had anticipated.

Those that survive reflect just how vulnerable mountain glaciers have become as global temperatures rise . Where glaciers once covered large expanses of the western mountains thousands of years ago, most of the remaining glaciers in the Rockies and Sierra Nevada are small and found in topographically protected places.

When people think of glaciers, they often picture huge ice streams with icebergs calving off the front, like you’ll find in Alaska or Greenland. In the Lower 48 states, with the exception of a few large glaciers in Washington, they’re much smaller.

We found that the average glacier area is about one-tenth of a square mile (about a quarter of a square kilometer) in size. The area of the largest glacier, found on Washington’s Mount Rainier, is about 4.3 square miles (11.24 square kilometers).

I was surprised to find that glaciers in the Rocky Mountains – those in Colorado, Montana and Wyoming and in the Sierra Nevada of California – subsist because of their unique position on the landscape, which somewhat insulates them from the otherwise less-favorable regional climate.

The surviving Rocky Mountain glaciers inhabit shaded niches less exposed to direct sunshine and gain additional snow from avalanches. If these glaciers were exposed to more sun and less snow accumulation, they likely wouldn’t exit at all.

Unlike the signature flamboyance seen with most other Yamaha bikes, the Xenter E has a relatively toned-down appearance. That approach seems deliberate, as Xenter E is largely positioned as a utilitarian vehicle. That said, the scooter does have a sleek design, featuring a distinctive front apron, a compact hexagonal-shaped headlamp and a vertically stacked DRL element.

Other key features include a lightweight front fender, step-up seat design, ‘Xenter E’ badging on the side panel and a broad rear fender. Primary USP is of course the large 16-inch alloy wheels. These are paired with 100/80 front and 120/80 rear tyres. Big-wheel scooters are preferred in Europe, as they can deliver a smoother riding experience over cobbled roads, tram lines and potholes.

In India, similar purposes are largely served by motorcycles. Most scooters here max out at around 14-inch wheel size, as evident from examples such as the Aerox 155, Xoom 160, SXR 175 GT and ADV160. Colour options for the Xenter E include Platinum Silver and Midnight Black. Yamaha has already announced a range of accessories for the scooter.

Yamaha Xenter E’s performance is comparable to a 125cc petrol-powered scooter. It is equipped with a fixed 3.5 kWh lithium-ion battery pack, offering a range of 67 miles or approximately 108 km. A new propulsion setup has been used, which is being referred to as an ‘eAxle’ unit. It comprises an air cooled permanent magnet motor, a controller and a reduction gear.

This setup is integrated as a single unit and mounted on the frame. Xenter E generates 10 bhp and 33.35 Nm of max torque. Power to the rear wheel is supplied via a belt drive. To ensure a flat floorboard and some underseat storage, Xenter E uses an L-shaped battery.

Adequate protection for the battery has been ensured with the use of a protective housing. Moreover, the battery is IP67-rated against water and dust. The scooter comes with an 800 watt onboard charger, which takes around 5.5 hours to achieve a full charge from zero. Users will also be able to charge the scooter at public charging networks by using Yamaha’s ‘YOU Charge’ subscription, which will be launched in early 2027.

Yamaha has used a new underbone frame for Xenter E. The scooter has a seat height of 790 mm, which is optimal for most users. Telescopic forks at the front offer 100 mm of suspension travel, whereas the rear dual shock absorbers have 97 mm of travel. Braking setup comprises 245 mm discs at the front and rear, integrated with ABS. Depending on their needs, users can choose from riding modes of S, T and E.

Lamborghini built its 20,000th Huracan in 2022 eight years after it had replaced the earlier Gallardo , which had needed a decade on the market to reach 14,022 units sold. The original Huracan LP 610-4 was shown at the Geneva Motor Show in March of 2014. It had an aluminum and carbon fiber hybrid chassis, a 5.2 liter V10 rated at 602 bhp at 8,250 rpm and 413 lb ft of torque at 6,500 rpm, a 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox and all-wheel-drive. Performante, EVO, STO, Tecnica and Sterrato versions followed and the last was the STJ, limited to just 10 cars. The V8 plug-in hybrid Temerario was unveiled as its successor in August 2024.

Lamborghini’s earlier GT3 cars had come from outside the factory. Reiter Engineering, a German privateer, developed and built the Gallardo GT3s, and the 2013 Gallardo GT3 FL2 was a joint project with Lamborghini. Lamborghini presented the Huracan GT3 at Sant’Agata Bolognese in early-2015 as its first GT3 car developed in-house, by its Squadra Corse motorsport department. It was a huge step for the Italian automaker.

In 2026 the company said this first in-house GT3 car had shared a strong technical relationship with its sister car in the Audi Group. Dallara worked on the aerodynamics, and its founder, Gian Paolo Dallara, was directly involved in the development. The ex-works price was €369,000 (about $427,000 USD), and that was before taxes.

Much like the Huracán road car, the GT3 had a hybrid body shell that was mainly aluminum, with carbon fiber reinforcement where torsional loads are highest. An FIA roll cage running back to the rear axle stiffened it further, and the composite body panels used quick-release fasteners.

The road car drives all four wheels, but the race car sent power to the rear wheels only through a pneumatically shifted 6-speed sequential gearbox from Hör and a mechanical locking differential. Double wishbones with uniball joints located all four wheels, with two-way adjustable Öhlins dampers.

title: Europe's electric car sales jump 49% as global EV sales grow
raw_summary: Global EV sales climbed 8% in October, with Europe’s battery electric vehicle (BEV) sales jumping 49% and North America posting its first year-over-year increase in 2026. But that North American rebound comes with a big catch. Drivers bought 2.09 million EVs worldwide last month, according to new data from Benchmark Mineral Intelligence . article_paragraphs: Global EV sales climbed 8% in October, with Europe’s battery electric vehicle (BEV) sales jumping 49% and North America posting its first year-over-year increase in 2026. But that North American rebound comes with a big catch.

Drivers bought 2.09 million EVs worldwide last month, according to new data from Benchmark Mineral Intelligence . That’s down 3% from September, but it brings sales for the first 10 months of 2026 to 17.5 million – up 5% from the same period last year.
Benchmark’s figures include both BEVs and plug-in hybrids (PHEVs) in the passenger-car and light-duty vehicle markets.
Europe sold 510,000 EVs in October, up 36% year over year. Fully electric cars did most of the work: BEV sales rose 49%, while plug-in hybrids grew 7%.
That puts October’s growth ahead of Europe’s 31% increase for the year so far. The region has now sold 4.5 million EVs in 2026.

Sales fell 17% from September’s record, but September got a boost from the UK’s twice-yearly registration plate change. The year-over-year figures give a clearer view of how quickly the market is growing.

Germany’s EV share topped 45% of new car sales, its highest level since December 2022. That earlier peak came as buyers rushed to get cars before subsidy cuts took effect. Fully electric car sales in Germany rose almost 80% from a year earlier to more than 95,000.

UK EV sales increased 30%. That’s particularly notable because the Electric Car Grant was already available in October 2025, although fewer models qualified then. So this growth comes against a market that was already getting government support.

article_paragraphs: Soon, there will be a third VW Group vehicle using the iconic turbocharged 2.5-liter inline-five, and it won't have an RS badge. Instead, these spy shots show that Cupra may be building a flagship Terramar VZ5, which follows in the footsteps of the Formentor VZ5 using the same potent engine as the Audi RS3 .

There's little to differentiate the striking Terramar VZ5 prototype in these images from other existing models, including the Terramar VZe , and that seems to be the point. The five-cylinder Formentor VZ5 looks largely identical to lesser models, making it a bit of a sleeper, and the same could be true for the Terramar VZ5. While the design of the new 2.5-liter Terramar may not stand out, our spy photographers claim this tester filled the air around the Nürburgring with the characteristic sound of the turbo five-cylinder.

Earlier this year, it was reported that Audi will be forced to kill off the RS3 in the third quarter of 2027 as it will fail to meet Euro 7 emissions regulations, but the 2.5-liter mill could be given a lifeline in less stringent markets, including the U.S. This should allow Audi to keep producing it beyond the RS3's demise, and the automaker has also expressed a willingness to explore electrifying the five-cylinder engine if it allows it to meet European regulations.

In the new Terramar VZ5, this engine should be just as punchy as it is in the Formentor VZ5. This means an impressive 384 horsepower and 354 pound-feet (480 Nm) of torque, routed to all four wheels through a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission. Beyond its impressive power and torque figures, the five-cylinder is beloved for its sound, and this alone should transform the driving experience. The sprint to 62 mph (100 kph) should be completed in around 4.2 seconds, which isn't quite as quick as the Audi RS3, but it's still impressive.

The most obvious visual difference between the existing Formentor VZ5 and other versions is the stacked quad exhaust system, configured much like the old Lexus ISF and Ferrari California. Curiously, this Terramar VZ5 prototype doesn't have this same design and appears to sport the same regular four tailpipes as other variants like the VZ and VZe. It's possible this could change for the production model.

The front is all familiar and has the same dark gray grille and air intakes as other Terramar offerings. Similarly, the wheels don't appear special, nor do the brakes, which continue to include bronze-painted front calipers. Global production of the Formentor VZ5 is capped at just 4,000 units. It's possible Cupra will also limit production of the Terramar VZ5, though this has yet to be confirmed. Whatever the case may be, the new SUV is expected to debut in early 2027.

title: The MGS6 Is A Great Electric SUV, But It Doesn't Stand Out
raw_summary: For Australians, there's never been a better time to be in the market for an all-electric, mid-size SUV. article_paragraphs: For Australians, there's never been a better time to be in the market for an all-electric, mid-size SUV. Just a few short years ago, the Tesla Model Y was the only competitive option in this segment. Now, a dizzying array of new entrants from China have arrived, each attempting to snatch the crown from the Model Y, which comfortably remains the nation's best-selling EV.

The 2026 MGS6 is one of the newer arrivals, produced by MG Motor — a division of China's SAIC Motor. The Chinese brand put the local EV market on notice when it launched the affordable MG4 in late 2023 as one of the nation's cheapest EVs. It has since expanded its range and moved upmarket with the MGS6, competing not only against the Model Y but also aiming to take the fight to the BYD Sealion 7, Zeekr 7X , Jaecoo J5, Kia EV5, and Hyundai Elexio.

Eager to see if it gets anywhere close to these models, we had the chance to live with the MGS6 for a week. It proved itself to be just as impressive as some of its compatriots while also serving as a compelling alternative to rivals from legacy brands. It's not perfect, however.

Two versions of the MGS6 are available for 2026. The entry-level EV Essence RWD is priced from AU$49,990 ($35,100) and comes equipped with a 77-kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt battery and promises up to 530 km (329 miles) of range on the WLTP range. Sitting above it is the EV Essence AWD, which we drove, starting at AU$56,990 ($40,000). It uses the same battery but has two electric motors, delivering a combined 266 kW (357 hp) and 540 Nm (398 lb-ft) of torque.

Unlike some competitors, including the Zeekr 7X, the MGS6 uses a 400-volt electrical architecture and DC charging tops out at 144 kW. That's a shame as it means charging from 10-80% takes 38 minutes, while many competitors can charge in less than 20 minutes. The added power of the all-wheel drive model also reduces the combined driving range to 485 km (301 miles).

Although MG under Chinese ownership first made a name for itself with budget and basic combustion-powered hatchbacks and SUVs, the 2026 MGS6 is a more premium product. This is immediately evident when you step into the cabin, as it reveals itself to be spacious, stylish, and well-appointed, just as it needs to be to compete in this market. And family buyers will be pleased to know that the second row is excellent and spacious enough for teenagers and adults.

The two displays -– a 10.25-inch digital gauge cluster and a 12.8-inch infotainment screen -– are smaller than some of the competition, but they definitely don't feel dated. Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are supported, although we experienced multiple disconnects with the Android Auto.

MG's homegrown software has been well-designed and is simple to use, but on vehicle start-up, it takes a while for the displays to turn on, which is a bit of an annoyance. Perhaps the best thing about the MG system isn't a feature it has, but rather something it doesn't have. MG has opted not to include all the climate controls into the screen. Instead, there are physical fan speed and temperature dials positioned below the central air vents.

article_paragraphs: We're not sure how the dealer thought they'd get away with it

Buying a car is one of the most financially important choices a person in America can make. That makes the entire situation hit a little harder when you hear that 47 people bought used cars in Massachusetts, only to find out that they couldn't legally register them. That's all because the person who sold those cars did so, in part, by grifting the buyers and the original seller. Now, that person is facing several years in prison and over $340,000 worth of restitution.

That man is Edward Cicciu, former owner of Bristol County Auto Exchange in Swansea, Massachusetts. He entered a plea of guilty in court on November 6. He's awaiting sentencing but will face at least four years in prison, and that number could jump to six. Either way, he'll deal with five years of probation and a restitution bill of $340,380.76 that will go to his 47 victims.

Cicciu doesn't appear to be the sharpest spoon in the drawer. Authorities say that he would mislead people through his business, Bristol County Auto Exchange. Customers initially complained that they were paying for cars but never getting the titles that they needed to register said vehicles . His genius scheme was to scam two parties. First, he would buy the car in question from an auction house. That auction house wouldn't release the title until he paid for the vehicle in full.

Meanwhile, he would sell the same vehicle to the customer and simply never pay the auction house. So the auction house would never send the title, the customer would never get the title, and Cicciu seemingly figured nobody would ever figure this daft idea out.

Police say that, "On Friday, CICCIU changed his plea to guilty on 43 counts of Larceny Over $1,200 by False Pretenses, 38 counts of Failure to Deliver Title Upon Transfer of a Motor Vehicle, 37 counts of Forging/Misusing an RMV Document, five counts of Larceny of a Motor Vehicle and two counts of Larceny by Check Over $1,200."

That's progress, but there's an important caveat. The restitution doesn't automatically mean that every victim will be made whole. Depending on the situation, some victims might have to go after Cicciu on their own. That said, the conviction could make that considerably easier.

The local DA and police chief had plenty to say on the subject. "The defendant conned and ripped off 47 victims between the ages of 18 and 80 who thought they were purchasing vehicles in a legitimate business transaction. Unfortunately, much to their horror, the defendant had no intention of completing the sales," said District Attorney Quinn.

It’s available in battery electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains, with prices starting at 139,900 yuan (about $21,000) for the plug-in hybrid and 149,900 yuan (around $22,500) for the fully electric version.
Both versions measure 5,080 mm long, 1,960 mm wide, and 1,495 mm high, with a 2,960 mm wheelbase, which is slightly longer than the Toyota Camry.
Don’t let the price fool you, however, the vehicle is packed with BYD’s latest breakthrough technology.
The new Seal 07 EV uses a 76.7 kWh second-generation BYD Blade LFP battery that provides a CLTC range of up to 481 miles (775 km).

Thanks to the second-gen Blade Batteries and BYD’s Flash Charging technology, the vehicle’s battery can charge from 10% to 70% in just five minutes. A full recharge, or going from 10% to 97%, takes just nine minutes.
The Seal 07 is also BYD’s first vehicle to debut with its new Disus-M Intelligent Magnetorheological Body Control System.

raw_summary: I saw last week that one of the biggest factors contributing to the enormous blue tsunami that set new history for US elections was people being fed up with government corruption. This has always been an issue to some extent, but corruption of the past versus corruption under Trump was like a wasp nest on the side of the house compared to a killer-hornet plague terrorizing the whole country (or continent, or globe). There is no comparison in US history that comes close to the corruption we’ve seen under the Trump administration. My assumption was that inflation — specifically coming from Trump’s war on Iran and Trump’s widespread tariffs — and a poor economy were the top reasons for the blue tsunami. However, I’ve since seen more surveys showing that corruption was either the biggest or second biggest factor in the strong swing to the left in the recent midterm elections.

title: KTM Reveals a New X-Bow Side-by-Side with a 330-HP Audi Engine
raw_summary: About 20 years ago, KTM—an Austrian manufacturer best known in the United States for its motorcycles—broke into the sports car business with the KTM X-Bow. Now, the KTM X-Bow brand is doing some expanding of its own with a new premium side-by-side powered by an Audi engine and priced at up to nearly $100K. KTM’s sports cars have historically used engines from the Volkswagen Group, and the new Arrow off-roader doesn’t break the mold. An Audi-sourced EA888 2.0-liter turbo four pairs with a seven-speed DSG transmission. The standard engine makes 280 horsepower, but the higher-priced Arrow Black Limited Edition is good for 330 horses. The EA888 is also used in the Audi A3 and S3, along with the GTI and R versions of the Volkswagen Golf. The X-Bow’s horsepower rating also beats the 2027 Polaris RZR Pro R , which tops out at 275 horses. That’s a pretty rowdy setup in the world of side-by-sides.

The X-Bow’s horsepower rating also beats the 2027 Polaris RZR Pro R , which tops out at 275 horses. That’s a pretty rowdy setup in the world of side-by-sides.

Front and rear limited-slip differentials, along with a chromoly steel chassis, help both Arrow variations fit right into Dakar-worthy off-road expeditions. A suspension with unequal-length control arms and dampers developed with KW Reiger allows for about 23.6 inches of travel.

Inside, both versions get Sabelt seats and harnesses. The standard Arrow variant features an open chassis, while the Black Limited Edition adds an enclosed cabin and air conditioning for even more comfort, as well as a fly-off handbrake for extra fun.

But air conditioning, race-inspired handbrakes, and 50 extra horses come at a cost. The Arrow Black Limited Edition will be limited to just 500 units, and it’ll only be available through a reservation process, which opens on November 17. The Black Limited Edition runs just under six figures with a starting price of $98,600.

After the Black Limited Edition goes on sale, the standard Arrow models will hit the market at $59,800. Sure, you could buy a brand new GTI, Golf R, S3, or A3 for less money, but they certainly couldn’t go where the Arrow could. KTM X-Bow says first deliveries are expected to start in late 2027.

Alayna Wilkening grew up reading motorsport magazines and following her grandpa around his Chevrolet dealership's showroom floor. In true Hoosier fashion, her first car was a hot pink custom cardboard "Fiero-vette" for her kindergarten Kindy 500 race. She now autocrosses a 1994 Miata with her dad, which she learned to drive the night before her first event. Alayna went to Indiana University and graduated with a degree in journalism and a minor in graphic design. As a testament to her great taste in cars, her first real one was a metallic orange 2007 Chevy HHR, which she lovingly called "The Dumptruck."

raw_title: Over One-Third Of Audi Nuvolari Production Will Be Sold In The U.S.
title: Over One-Third Of Audi Nuvolari Production Will Be Sold In The U.S
raw_summary: The 2027 Audi Nuvolari isn't a successor to the R8 because whereas that supercar was mass-produced in the tens of thousands over 18 years and two generations, just 499 Nuvolaris will ever be made. Audi has now announced that 182 of those are earmarked for the U.S., which means 36.5% of all Nuvolaris will land stateside, or one in every 2.74 cars. Each will go for an official starting price of $700,000 before destination or taxes, and U.S. deliveries are scheduled to start in the first half of 2028. That's almost twice as much money as the Lamborghini Temerario on which it's based, but the Lambo isn't limited production or quite as special. Despite the numbered production run and how this sort of car tends to sell out before the public even knows about it, Audi of America says there are still build slots available, as "orders continue to be accepted at authorized Audi dealerships throughout the United States for a limited time."

Sharing its powertrain with the Temerario , the Audi Nuvolari uses a twin-turbo 4.0-liter V8 and three axial-flux hybrid electric motors to make 987 horsepower combined. 0 to 60 mph happens in just 2.5 seconds, and its top speed stands at 217 mph. It's said to use Formula 1-derived tech — Audi is in F1 now, in case you forgot — in the hybrid energy management system, by-wire brakes, active aero, and launch control programming.

It's also a new luxury performance car that manages to look good and original without being "polarizing." It's brutalist and a departure from existing Audi styling, but most colleagues I've talked to about it view its design favorably. For what it's worth, I think it's hella cool, particularly from the rear three-quarter view. Audi says there are 50 gloss paint colors and over 10 matte finishes, but you can of course make it look however you want with Audi Exclusive. You can get Audi's first exposed carbon-fiber body on the Nuvolari, and on the inside there's dozens more options.

In any case, if you're in the States and have 700 grand to splash on a German supercar (or, let's be real, almost a million after accounting for options, fees and taxes), there's apparently still time to go to your local Audi dealership and put your name down for a Nuvolari. You'd be joining a small club that only 181 other Americans will be a part of.

article_paragraphs: Kia became the first non-European brand to score a hat trick at the 2026 Golden Steering Wheel Awards, Germany’s most prestigious auto awards.
The Korean automaker won a triple crown at the 2026 Golden Steering Wheel Awards, with the EV2, K4 Sportswagon, and EV5 taking first in their class.
This is the first time a non-European brand has won three Golden Steering Wheel Awards in a single year in the prestigious award’s 50-year history.

The award is organized by AUTO BILD and BILD am SONNTAG with 90 new models nominated this year. Readers chose 27 finalists, three in each of the nine classes, which were then tested by a panel of celebrities and auto experts.

The judges tested the vehicles at the DEKRA-Lausitzring racetrack. Vehicles were judged on handling, comfort, ease of use, quality, and everyday practicality, as well as the sustainability and value they offer.
Kia won across three very different categories with the fully electric EV2 and EV5, alongside the gas-powered K4 Sportswagon.

The EV2, Kia’s entry-level electric SUV, won the award for the “Best Car Under €30,000.” Developed specifically for Europe, the compact EV is only 4.06 meters long, but offers up to 403 liters of cargo space.
It also offers a WLTP driving range of up to 453 km (281 miles), which is among the longest in its class.

title: Our Long-Term Ram 1500 Taught Us to Love Hurricanes
raw_summary: Our expectations for the Ram 1500 are well established. This being the third 1500 of the current generation we’ve put through a long-term test, the only real question mark was under the hood. For 2025, Ram pulled the Hemi V-8 from the lineup. article_paragraphs: Our expectations for the Ram 1500 are well established. This being the third 1500 of the current generation we’ve put through a long-term test, the only real question mark was under the hood.

For 2025, Ram pulled the Hemi V-8 from the lineup. In its place came the Hurricane: a twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six making 420 horsepower and 469 pound-feet of torque in its base form. Sure, that’s more power than the Hemi produced, but some buyers hold V-8-powered full-size trucks as a fundamental truth, right next to basic arithmetic and gravity. These folks would probably dismiss the Ram’s twin-turbo six outright. Their loss.

Over 40,000 miles, our Big Horn 4x4 model was a six-passenger, 5765-pound workhorse for all manner of tasks: towing trailers, swallowing luggage, devouring interstate miles, and hauling the kind of oversize objects people buy because they have access to a pickup, a credit card, and a Costco membership.
See all results for used 2025 Ram 1500 for sale near 85225

With the Hurricane, the Ram proved smooth, strong, and surprisingly sophisticated, like a BMW wearing Carhartt. We loved its power too. Our initial testing logged 60 mph in 4.8 seconds and the quarter-mile in 13.6 seconds at 100 mph. That’s serious pace for a crew-cab pickup on Falken Wildpeak all-terrain tires, and it was 1.3 seconds quicker to 60 mph than the 395-hp 5.7-liter V-8–powered 2019 Ram 1500 we ran through a 40,000-mile test. Our 2025 example repeated its 60-mph time at 40,000 miles, though its quarter-mile effort slipped a little to 13.8 seconds at 96 mph. Still, leave it in rear-drive mode, and the traction-control light will occasionally flicker during moderate freeway acceleration in the wet. That is not a complaint.

Indeed, driving the Ram 1500 leads to few complaints, which is why it’s been on our 10Best list eight times. The 1500, with its four-corner coil-spring suspension, rode with the calm authority that has long separated this truck from its rear-leaf-spring competitors, cruising and towing with the ease of a long-legged Clydesdale at a trot and making you wonder why other pickups don’t ride this well.

The Ram was a happy mile eater, as the optional 33.0-gallon fuel tank regularly showed more than 500 miles of indicated range after a fill-up. The cabin was a great place to while away the hours. Ram has been doing excellent truck interiors long enough that the surprise has worn off, but the usefulness remains. The front bench gave us seating for six and a healthy dose of nostalgia, the rear seat offered limo-like sprawl-out space, and the front armrest placed a hand naturally in line with the shifter and stereo controls.

Our most vocal complaints fell on the large mirrors from the Trailer-Tow Group package. They were fantastic when there was a trailer behind you and a nuisance when there wasn’t, blocking entire cars at roundabouts and requiring chicken-like head bobbing to see around them.

raw_summary: The season of giving is almost here, and the perfect gift for the Batman fans in your life, or shamelessly just you, might be this very real Batpod. The Batman motorcycle, featured in Christopher Nolan's "The Dark Knight" and "The Dark Knight Rises" just so happens to be on on auction right now with Propstore , as part of its Entertainment Memorabilia Live Auction in London. The Batman motorcycle, featured in Christopher Nolan's "The Dark Knight" and "The Dark Knight Rises" just so happens to be on on auction right now with Propstore , as part of its Entertainment Memorabilia Live Auction in London. It also happens to close just in time to get it home and under whatever shrine you celebrate for the winter solstice.

Originally sold by Propstore in 2016 as part of its Entertainment Memorabilia Auction, this is the bike used in notable "The Dark Knight" moments such as when Batman (Christian Bale) evaded the Joker (Heath Ledger) , demonstrating the Batpod's abilities to climb walls and turn around without moving forward thanks to the wheels' ability to flip side-to-side, making the Hummer's crabwalking capabilities look like ancient technology. In "The Dark Knight Rises," Batman gave Catwoman (Anne Hathaway) the Batpod to use as a getaway vehicle while he took on Bane and the League of Shadows.

Batman's Batpod was born from the minds of Nolan and production designer for the films, Nathan Crowley, whose work has included "Wonka ," the "Wicked" films , Dunkirk ," " Westworld ," and "Interstellar." It was made to be an alternative for Batman's Tumbler, the armored-tank vehicle that happens to also be quite multi-faceted, like when it transformed into a heavy duty flight vehicle to escape Gotham Police as they cornered Batman in an alley. The man who brought the bike to life was Chris Corbould, who was special-effects supervisor for both films but might be best known for his work on the James Bond film series and "Inception," for which he won an Academy award.

The Batpod is being sold as-is, in non-functional, "rolling only" condition with no fluids, battery, fuel tank or throttle controls. You'd have to be fairly innovative to get it moving. That might be for the best, though, as the rider position is prone. If you were to pilot it, you'd be lying down in a stance more awkward than a MotoGP rider and more like a sprint stance used in spinning classes, then forced to steer with your arms and shoulders. At least there is a little bit of black foam lining the body, saddle, and knee rests to give your body a little respite.

The custom-fabricated chassis wears 31-inch Hoosier racing tires and a Honda 750 engine. Its cannon barrels are made of plastic, resin and fiberglass, and it also has a light-up laser-targeting unit above the right hand grip, which doesn't actually work. Despite its nonworking state, it at least bears some battle scars from its use in scenes between both movies.

Included in the sale is a custom metal support stand for display, as well as a certificate of authenticity from Warner Brothers. Bids for this Hero Batpod close December 4 at 10:00 a.m. EST. As of this writing bids sit at around $300,000, with Propstore estimating the sale to range between around $600,000 to $1.2 million. If that's too rich for your taste, maybe you could look into building your own Batpod .

title: The $700,000 Audi Nuvolari Will Be Extremely Rare in the U.S
raw_summary: Three years after the death of the R8 , Audi revealed a new supercar. First shown in June, the Nuvolari wears a brutalist design and borrows the Lamborghini Temerario’s 789-hp twin-turbo V-8, mating it with a trio of electric motors for a total of 987 horsepower. Unlike the R8, though, the Nuvolari will be a limited-production affair, and now we know just how many will make it to the United States, and what they’ll cost when they get here. The R8, which lasted from 2007 to 2023, was a true series production car, but Audi only plans on building 499 units of the Nuvolari. Of that total, just 182 will reach the United States. Once they do, each of their new owners will have to pony up at least $700,000. That figure doesn’t include the designation fee, which Audi has yet to disclose.

The lucky few who get to park a Nuvolari in their garage (or more likely a supercar-filled warehouse) will have to be patient. Deliveries won’t start until the first half of 2028, but once owners get their hands on the Nuvolari, we imagine they will be quite happy. That 987-hp powertrain propels the distinctively designed supercar to 60 mph in a claimed 2.5 seconds and to a top speed of 217 mph, making it both the most powerful and fastest production Audi ever.

Given that the Nuvolari has only been shown so far in a matte gray hue, we look forward to seeing what it looks like in more vibrant colors.

raw_title: SpaceX Wants To Build Data Center Powered By Its Newest Product: Natural Gas
title: SpaceX Wants To Build Data Center Powered By Its Newest Product: Natural Gas
raw_summary: SpaceX filed its intention to build a new AI data center at its facility in Starbase, Texas, which will be powered by a new natural gas plant that it will also build. None of that sounds like space, but this is the company that SpaceX has become. The initial phase of this build-out is projected to cost $24 billion, though more phases are to come. Critically, this gives the rocket company, which is also an internet company, which is also an AI company, which is also a social media company, a way to make use of its newest product: natural gas. Again, space! The company has been moving towards an expansion into fossil fuels for the last few months. In June, SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell said the company was making plans for "basically mining our own natural gas... to develop our own propellant and bring it to the rocket." The rocket in question being Starship, which SpaceX is essentially betting its future on . That takes a mixture of methane and liquid oxygen to fire up its thrusters; methane can be extracted from natural gas. For that reason, the company has made major moves to ensure its own supply. It hired for its own natural gas trader, normally an oil industry job for buying and selling the stuff, and is building its own pipelines in both Florida and Texas, per Bloomberg .

It hired for its own natural gas trader, normally an oil industry job for buying and selling the stuff, and is building its own pipelines in both Florida and Texas, per Bloomberg .

In addition, SpaceX rapidly spun up AI data centers in Tennessee and Mississippi earlier this year, powered by, you guessed it, natural gas. It spun them up so rapidly that the company is now being sued for ignoring environmental laws . SpaceX is apparently trying to go fast again for this new Texas endeavor, likely trying to get things rolling before a newer, bluer state government takes over . SpaceX wants to grab both the air pollution permits it needs plus a few tax breaks; Texas is expected to make both harder to get early next year, per Politico . To that end, Starbase's city government will convene on the matter in December. There's good reason to think the company will get what it wants: two of the city's three commission members are SpaceX executives. That's handy.

As for the power plant itself, it will feature 35 mobile natural gas turbines and produce around 750 megawatts of electricity. So it's now in the business of building power plants, buying and trading natural gas, and laying out pipelines, all in service of the enough data centers it's putting up. No wonder Vice President of Launch Kiko Dontchev is now saying , "Fundamentally we are an infrastructure company at this point." You don't say, Dontchev.

At this point, it's not too much of a stretch to say that SpaceX is just the Elon Musk Show, going into whatever industry he feels like at the moment. If his long-desired merger with Tesla goes through, then it will really just be a conglomerate with all sorts of fingers in all sorts of pies. Space will still be a part of what SpaceX does, but now that AI is earning it more revenue than rockets , it may become a smaller and smaller part. Mars has never looked so far away.

raw_summary: Great news everyone! We just set another new record, and this time it has nothing to do with diesel prices . Sadly, though, it isn't nearly as cool as the Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X destroying the Pikes Peak production car record over the summer. No, unfortunately for everyone who still has to work for a living, Kelley Blue Book reports the average transaction price for new cars hasn't just crossed the $50,000 mark. That's 1.3% higher than it was in September and a 2.1% increase year-over-year.
