Sadly, though, it isn't nearly as cool as the Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X destroying the Pikes Peak production car record over the summer. No, unfortunately for everyone who still has to work for a living, Kelley Blue Book reports the average transaction price for new cars hasn't just crossed the $50,000 mark. In October, the average transaction price rose to a level never before seen in the U.S. So that's pretty exciting. Aren't you thrilled to be alive right now to experience it?

Using data from its parent company, Cox Automotive, KBB says the average price consumers paid for new cars in the U.S. hit $51,109 in the month of October. That's 1.3% higher than it was in September and a 2.1% increase year-over-year. Higher prices aren't usually a good thing, especially when those higher prices are on things most people need to use every day (cars) instead of luxuries that you don't have to own to participate in society. The average MSRP of new vehicles is also up, reportedly hitting $52,933 in October, up 1.4% versus September and 2.4% higher year-over-year.

That said, it isn't all bad news. There's always a silver lining, and this time around, KBB says, "The Kelley Blue Book ATP estimate marked an all-time high even as vehicle price inflation in October was below long-term averages." Yes, you read that right. The average price people are paying for new cars hit an all-time high in October, but at least the rate of inflation isn't as high as it could be. Don't you feel grateful for that? I know I do. From the sound of it, dealers are also perfectly happy to let customers pay those high prices, as opposed to chasing faster turnover:

The higher ATP – an estimate of the average product prices paid in October before all available incentives, taxes and fees are factored in – was driven in part by both price inflation and strong sales of expensive midsize and full-size SUVs and full-size pickup trucks. Incentive spending increased modestly in October but remains below long-term averages, suggesting automakers and dealers are not aggressively pursuing sales and inventory reduction, despite record prices.

KBB also found that incentive spending accounted for 6.8% of ATP in October. With September 2026 at 6.7% and October 2025 at 6.5%, incentives are trending upward but it's been slow and doesn't appear to have contributed significantly to October's ATP record. Plus, not every car costs the same, and some segments will naturally cost less to buy than others. Once you break pricing out by segment, only one really feels like an outlier. Here's how KBB's breakdown looks:

As you can see, midsize SUVs were number one in sales volume and had an ATP of $50,570, but the people buying compact cars only paid $28,000 for them on average. That probably seems high for a compact, but remember, a 2027 Nissan Sentra without any options has an MSRP of almost $25,000 with destination, and an extra $3,000 to drive something nicer than a stripped-out, base-model Sentra sounds pretty fair to me.

Meanwhile, full-size pickup trucks placed third behind midsize and compact SUVs, but the average transaction price is close to double what people are paying for Honda CR-Vs and Hyundai Tucsons. Yes, on average , full-size truck buyers pay $67,912 for their trucks. Some Ford F-150s will cost more, some Chevrolet Silverados will cost less, but on average a full-size pickup truck buyer spent more than $65,000 to buy their truck.

That said, it's also worth reminding everyone that if you adjust for inflation, the 1997 Toyota Camry cost more than a brand new 2026 Camry does today . Truck buyers' obsession with expensive trucks skews the average, but if raises had kept up with inflation, it wouldn't be nearly as scary to hear the Camry now starts at $30,995. Cars haven't gotten too expensive. Our bosses denying us raises has simply left us too poor to afford these new cars. Meanwhile, they're out there buying $70,000 trucks like its nothing. Or at least they did before Woke 3 arrived . Maybe under Woke 3, we're all getting raises.

title: BYD's full-size luxury SUV has a wheel problem, and it's fixing it for free
raw_summary: BYD is apologizing after a supplier error left some owners of its new full-size flagship SUV with the wrong wheels. The Great Tang, or Da Tang as it’s called in China, is the first flagship D-segment SUV under its Dynasty series, the largest and most luxurious SUV from the lineup.
summary: BYD is apologizing after a supplier error left some owners of its new full-size flagship SUV with the wrong wheels. The Great Tang, or Da Tang as it’s called in China, is the first flagship D-segment SUV under its Dynasty series, the largest and most luxurious SUV from the lineup.
article_paragraphs: BYD is apologizing after a supplier error left some owners of its new full-size flagship SUV with the wrong wheels.
The Great Tang, or Da Tang as it’s called in China, is the first flagship D-segment SUV under its Dynasty series, the largest and most luxurious SUV from the lineup.
After opening preorders at the Beijing Auto Show in April, BYD said the high-end SUV secured over 30,000 preorders in 24 hours. Two weeks later, preorders reached over 100,000.
By the time it went on sale in mid-June, over 150,000 buyers had preordered the Great Tang, marking a new record for a single BYD model.

While it has been the top-selling pure electric large SUV for two months, with more than 10,000 sold since it hit the market, BYD issued an apology on November 11 for fitting the wrong front and rear wheel rims on some Great Tang models.
The apology comes after several owners complained that the wheels were improperly installed on their vehicles.
BYD said the issue stemmed from a coding error by the wheel mesh assembly supplier, which led to incorrect assembly on some Great Tang vehicles.

The company said it “immediately” launched an investigation and corrected the issue so newly built vehicles will not be affected. In addition, the supplier introduced a new visual error-prevention mechanism to limit issues like this going forward.

title: Tesla extends Cybertruck production to late summer 2027 amid fan backlash
raw_summary: Elon Musk now says Tesla will keep building the Cybertruck “through the end of summer 2027” to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” That buys the electric pickup roughly two to three more months, five days after Tesla first announced it was killing it. The reprieve lands as a growing number of Tesla’s own fans push back on the decision, and on what it says about Tesla’s future as a company that sells cars to people.
summary: Elon Musk now says Tesla will keep building the Cybertruck “through the end of summer 2027” to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” That buys the electric pickup roughly two to three more months, five days after Tesla first announced it was killing it.
article_paragraphs: Elon Musk now says Tesla will keep building the Cybertruck “through the end of summer 2027” to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” That buys the electric pickup roughly two to three more months, five days after Tesla first announced it was killing it.
The reprieve lands as a growing number of Tesla’s own fans push back on the decision, and on what it says about Tesla’s future as a company that sells cars to people.

On November 6, Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas “around the middle of next year” to make room for Cybercab. On November 9, he wrote the line would shut “in about 8 months” and that Tesla would “have to return deposits for a lot of people.” Now it’s the end of summer.
In order to work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog, production will be extended through the end of summer 2027

The reasons have moved around just as much. First it was factory space, then “a very limited number of smart, dedicated people,” then the “opportunity cost” of the truck’s complexity. We went through each of them: Tesla is ending the Cybertruck as sales stall at about 10% of plan , Musk’s demand claim doesn’t survive the numbers , and Musk admitted Tesla doesn’t have the talent to run more than one vehicle program .

And the “backlog” is one Tesla built itself. Before the announcement, the truck was selling at a pace of roughly 30,000 units a year, about 10% of the 250,000 Tesla planned for, on a line with over 125,000 units of installed capacity. Telling people the truck is going away creates a last-call rush. That’s not demand Tesla was missing before.
Tesla also raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% the same day and paused orders for the base Dual Motor. The cheapest Cybertruck you can order is now $92,490, up from $69,990 in early August.

Some of the people in that backlog have been waiting a while. Several cheering in Musk’s replies say they’re still waiting on the $59,990 Cybertruck Tesla sold for “10 days only” in February. One asked whether Tesla will prioritize Premium and Cyberbeast orders over theirs. Musk didn’t answer.

title: New Lotus Supercar's 670-HP Twin-Turbo V8 Revealed By Powertrain Supplier Horse
raw_summary: Back in May, Lotus announced that it would be introducing a new supercar for 2028 . Known as the Type 135, it will be a blank-sheet development and get a hybrid V8 powertrain making more than 986 horsepower (or 1,000 metric horses) combining electricity and internal combustion. The company's new powertrain supplier, Horse — yes, that's the company's name — has now revealed details of what'll power the car much of automotive media has unofficially took to calling the new Esprit. Lotus' first proper supercar will use an engine called the Horse W40, a twin-turbo 4.0-liter V8 making more than 670 hp and 590 lb-ft of torque by itself. Weighing 441 pounds, this V8 is engineered for longitudinal layouts and has its two turbos mounted on top in a "hot-V" configuration — that's when the turbos sit inside the "V" of the engine, minimizing the distance gases have to travel and thereby minimizing turbo lag. Horse says the W40 makes "exceptional low-end torque along with high peak power" and is ideal for everything from sports cars to pickups and off-roaders, but of course it'd say that.

Horse says the W40 makes "exceptional low-end torque along with high peak power" and is ideal for everything from sports cars to pickups and off-roaders, but of course it'd say that.

This engine is also said to be designed from the get-go to work as part of a hybrid powertrain, and Horse also makes the 8-speed dual-clutch hybrid gearbox that it'll be paired to. Known as the Horse 8LDCT, this transmission can withstand up to 774 lb-ft of torque. It uses a "sports car-grade" wet dual-clutch, can pull of shifts in under 20 milliseconds, and gets a built-in silicon carbide control system and power module, plus a variable-displacement mechanical pump.

In case you're unfamiliar, Horse Powertrain is a joint venture between Renault and Lotus' Chinese parent company, Geely. Horse also happens to build that waterproof B20 four-cylinder that goes into Geely's floating Galaxy Cruiser 700 off-roader , and the W40 is the powertrain supplier's first V8.
Lotus says its new supercar is expected to be manufactured in Europe, get revealed in 2028, and start deliveries that same year.

raw_title: The Perovskite Solar Cell Kraken Has Been Unleashed Upon The US
title: The Perovskite Solar Cell Kraken Has Been Unleashed Upon The US
raw_summary: Perovskite is a relatively inexpensive material that has attracted thousands of researchers since 2009, when a team of scientists in Japan first demonstrated its use in solar cells. They achieved a solar energy conversion efficiency of little more than 3%, but since science loves a challenge, that was just the beginning of the story. In the latest chapter, the US firms Heliene and Caeulux have just introduced a new perovskite-enabled solar module that hits the jackpot at up to 27% efficiency, and it is already in commercial production, no less. So far in the renewable energy transition, silicon has shouldered much of the heavy lifting due to its excellent solar conversion properties. Still, silicon is relatively expensive material that demands a complex manufacturing process. Perovskite is the reverse. Based on a naturally occurring mineral, synthetic perovskites can be lab-grown and applied to solar cell fabrication in a high volume, high throughput process similar to roll-to-roll manufacturing and other solution-based methods (see lots more perovskite background here ).

article_paragraphs: Perovskite is a relatively inexpensive material that has attracted thousands of researchers since 2009, when a team of scientists in Japan first demonstrated its use in solar cells. They achieved a solar energy conversion efficiency of little more than 3%, but since science loves a challenge, that was just the beginning of the story. In the latest chapter, the US firms Heliene and Caeulux have just introduced a new perovskite-enabled solar module that hits the jackpot at up to 27% efficiency, and it is already in commercial production, no less.

So far in the renewable energy transition, silicon has shouldered much of the heavy lifting due to its excellent solar conversion properties. Still, silicon is relatively expensive material that demands a complex manufacturing process. Perovskite is the reverse. Based on a naturally occurring mineral, synthetic perovskites can be lab-grown and applied to solar cell fabrication in a high volume, high throughput process similar to roll-to-roll manufacturing and other solution-based methods (see lots more perovskite background here ).

There being no such thing as a free lunch, “raw” perovskite is challenged by natural conditions, namely, humidity. Tweaking the formula with other, more durable materials can resolve that problem. Researchers have also developed a tandem solution , in which a perovskite layer rests upon a silicon layer, providing an efficiency boost while minimizing the additional cost.

In the US solar market, the sticky wicket is the current state of federal energy, trade, and tax polices. Still, the red-hot demand for solar energy in the US has motivated solar stakeholders to steamroll over those obstacles, attracting overseas investors ( here’s one example) as well as new domestic ventures.

On the domestic side, the Corning-backed manufacturer Heliene has been focusing on silicon while the startup Caelux has tackled the perovskite solar cell challenge with a glass substrate that can be layered onto other materials in a solar module. Now the two manufacturers have combined forces, with Caelux’s perovskite-doped glass boosting the conversion efficiency of Heliene’s N-type solar cells by up to 20%.

The Caelux-Heliene mashup comes at a time when Congress has finally put the wheels in motion to streamline the permitting process for energy projects. The two firms already have a running head start. On November 10, the two firms announced that commercial-scale production has already begun on their Hybrid-Tandem™ solar module

“ Manufactured by Heliene in Minnesota, the perovskite plus silicon technology combines Caelux’s Energy Producing Glass with Heliene’s established silicon module platform to construct a solar module with two separate power generation layers that deliver higher power density,” Heliene explains.

“One of the advantages of Caelux’s technology is that we can integrate its Energy Producing Glass into our existing manufacturing lines without having to build an entirely new production setup,” added Martin Pochtaruk, Heliene CEO and Founder, in a press statement.

The post , published on the @tesla_semi account on X at noon ET today, shows four Semis lined up at sunset under the caption “Hello Windy City.” Tesla didn’t name the customer.
Hello Windy City Chicago’s first 50 Semis en route for delivery pic.twitter.com/75kig8yWsb

But the only 50-truck Semi order tied to Chicago belongs to HMD Trucking. The family-owned carrier was founded in Chicago in 1998, runs more than 650 trucks (almost all diesel), and ordered 50 Semis right after Tesla’s production event in September.

HMD took its first truck on November 2 and says it’s the first Tesla Semi registered in Illinois. COO Michael Mahler said Tesla “has been transparent with us regarding the capabilities of Semi every step of the way.”

The company ran a Semi for more than 4,000 miles over the summer and averaged 1.74 kWh per mile, right in line with Tesla’s 1.7 kWh/mile claim. The first trucks will mostly handle local runs around Chicago, and HMD is installing its own chargers there since Tesla’s Megacharger network is still concentrated along the I-5 and I-10 corridors in the West.

Owner Henry Malukas told MotorTrend the deal is worth about $15 million. That’s roughly $300,000 per truck, in line with the ~$290,000 Long Range pricing we reported when the first truck came off the high-volume line and a long way from the $180,000 Tesla advertised in 2017.

Under the failsafe mode, power steering is disabled, making the vehicle much harder to steer, and an EPS warning light appears in the instrument cluster. Honda was unable to replicate and name the issue until December 2025 due to dealers and suppliers deleting the error codes as part of their engine diagnostic process when affected cars were serviced.

Honda has received one injury report related to the defect, as well as 146 warranty claims, as of October 22. Owners of affected vehicles will receive notice in the mail by December 14, and should schedule an appointment with an authorized Honda or Acura dealer for a software update at no cost. In the meantime, owners can check the NHTSA recall website to see if their vehicle is involved.

title: 2027 Mercedes C-Class Follows The Formula And Sticks The Landing
raw_summary: As computers get cheaper , electronic features more important , and new automakers enter the U.S. market , it's harder to understand where each luxury brand positions itself. BMWs were traditionally the sporty ones, but with an adjustable suspension, you can make a sporty BMW feel luxurious. Is Genesis a value brand or a design brand? Who buys an Audi and why? article_paragraphs: As computers get cheaper , electronic features more important , and new automakers enter the U.S. market , it's harder to understand where each luxury brand positions itself. Mercedes, however, remains pretty easy to pigeonhole. It's the tech and luxury brand, whether you buy a six-figure GLS or a more affordable alternative, like the facelifted Mercedes-Benz C-Class .

If you don't like screens and wish Mercedes would go back to building the kinds of cars it did in the late 1980s, I'm sorry. The new C-Class probably isn't for you. Mercedes is looking forward, not back, and that means packing as much tech into its cars as it can. That may not be to your personal taste, but it does give Mercedes a clear identity. So even if you haven't driven the new C-Class, in some ways, you already know what to expect. You're going to get a comfortable, spacious luxury car with big screens, more features than you need or may even be able to remember, and all the refinement Mercedes can muster. It just doesn't hide its secrets.

Mercedes likes to call its cars "new" any time it updates them, but really, this is a refresh. That was also to be expected, since this W206 generation that first went on sale for the 2022 model year still hadn't received a mid-cycle refresh. Sometimes, an update means significant styling changes both inside and out, but here, Mercedes takes a more restrained approach. You get a bigger grille and the star headlights and taillights that we first saw on the CLA , but pretty much everything else about the exterior styling looks familiar. The new C-Class makes it clear from the start that you won't find too many mysteries or wild changes inside.

The car keeps its word, too. If you've driven the pre-facelift C-Class, you'll be right at home in the new one's largely unchanged cabin. That does mean it's time for the big screen haters to look away from the screens they're reading this on, because yes, Mercedes kept the 12.3-inch driver display and 11.9-inch infotainment touchscreen from the outgoing model. The big change is that it now features Mercedes' latest MB.OS infotainment system, which has AI built in. In fact, the new C-Class has multiple AIs built in, allowing you to get use ChatGPT, Gemini, or (for some reason) Bing.

The AI integration doesn't really add much to the experience, but if you use voice commands, the AI does process language more naturally and is more helpful as a result. Of course, you're still using AI, and that comes with a whole host of other ethical issues, but functionally, yes, it is better than before. Anyone who gave up on voice controls that were more frustrating to use than they were helpful may want to give them a try, though, because we're finally at a point where it isn't always easier to find the screen controls yourself.

The bigger story is the engineers upping the C-Class' processing power to the point that it qualifies as a supercomputer. That makes it possible for Mercedes to offer a more advanced version of its augmented reality head-up display, and it needed to upgrade the processing power before it could add its MB.Drive Assist Pro "Level 2++" advanced driver-assistance system that should rival Tesla's so-called Full Self-Driving, only made by a company that cares about safety. Still, if you're familiar with the previous version, the C-Class' infotainment system should feel incredibly familiar, so no need to worry about getting lost in menus or being forced to use the voice controls after giving up.

While the exterior styling helps keep the C-Class in line with other Mercedes models, and the software updates help keep the cabin current, you could also forgive someone who didn't know for not realizing Mercedes even updated its compact sedan. Still, I can't imagine that person would have any complaints about the fit and finish of the cabin, how comfortable it is, or how little noise intrudes once the doors are closed and the windows are up, which will be even more appreciated if you spring for the optional Burmester 3D surround-sound system with Dolby Atmos.

Since we were in Europe, Mercedes had us driving European models, which meant I had access to the wagon, a plug-in-hybrid powertrain, and more. The U.S., however, only gets the C350 for now, with a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-4 making the same 255 horsepower and 295 pound-feet of torque as the pre-facelift C300. Mercedes promises a 5.8-second 0-to-60-mph time with the help of its familiar 9-speed automatic transmission. That's not especially quick, but Mercedes-AMG will have more powerful versions coming before we know it — in fact, the brand has already confirmed the old four-cylinder C63 will be replaced by a six-cylinder model .

title: Urgent Safety Alert: Lincoln Recalls 37,000 Navigators Because The Front Seats Might Be Haunted
raw_summary: If the U.S. were a sane country, stores would be decorated for Thanksgiving right now , not covered in Santas and blasting Christmas music . But regardless of whether you properly appreciate our national eating holiday or insist on skipping straight to the materialist holiday, at least we can all agree spooky season should be behind us. Which is why we wish we'd caught Lincoln's latest Navigator recall last month when it was more on theme. You see, according to the recall, Lincoln's concerned some of its seats could basically become haunted. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration published the recall on October 20, less than two weeks before Halloween, but sadly, we missed it until our friends over at Car and Driver spotted it yesterday. Technically, neither Lincoln, NHTSA, nor Car and Driver used the word "haunted," but what other term are you supposed to use when the official description of the recall is literally, "Front Passenger Seat May Move Unexpectedly,"? Ghosts or no ghosts, those Navigator seats sound haunted, and you'll never convince me otherwise.

article_paragraphs: If the U.S. were a sane country, stores would be decorated for Thanksgiving right now , not covered in Santas and blasting Christmas music . Which is why we wish we'd caught Lincoln's latest Navigator recall last month when it was more on theme. You see, according to the recall, Lincoln's concerned some of its seats could basically become haunted.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration published the recall on October 20, less than two weeks before Halloween, but sadly, we missed it until our friends over at Car and Driver spotted it yesterday. Technically, neither Lincoln, NHTSA, nor Car and Driver used the word "haunted," but what other term are you supposed to use when the official description of the recall is literally, "Front Passenger Seat May Move Unexpectedly,"? Ghosts or no ghosts, those Navigator seats sound haunted, and you'll never convince me otherwise.

Per the information in the recall, Lincoln believes as many as 36,994 Navigators built for the 2025, 2026, and 2027 model years could be affected. Typically, though, recalls involve a large number of cars the automaker wants to check for a defect, even if only 1%-3% of the recalled vehicles will likely have any problems. This one's a little different, though, with the recall report estimating a whopping 100% estimated to have the defect. So if you own one of the affected Navigators, the dealer will probably have to fix it.

So what's NHTSA's theory? Well, it isn't ghosts, even though we know for a fact that it's definitely ghosts. Lincoln just doesn't want to spook everyone by confirming the supernatural is real. Officially, owners whose Navigators have the chauffeur package may notice their front passenger seat moving unexpectedly, and it's all because of your (kids') nasty, grubby little fingers. From the recall report:

Affected vehicles contain a "Chauffer Seat Feature" that can be accessed by a passenger in the rear seat via a second-row digital touchscreen console, known as the RACM. One action on this RACM is to allow the rear passenger the ability to move the front passenger seat in order to provide more legroom.

Residue left on the RACM can be registered as finger touch input allowing the front passenger seat to move unintentionally. Additionally, if the home screen button on the RACM is pressed at the same time the seat movement button is pressed, the seat may continue moving to its full travel limit without any additional input.

Personally, I still think ghosts are a more likely explanation than Cheeto fingers, but I guess you can't exactly put that in an official government recall. Could you imagine the civil unrest if the feds confirmed the existence of ghosts? Basically, what I'm saying is that you and I both know they're lying, but it's better to pretend there's a problem with the RACM. Faulty Lincolns, American can deal with. Haunted Lincolns? That's probably too much, all things considered.

After a false start, Vietnamese startup automaker VinFast is giving its VF9 electric mid-size SUV another go in the U.S. market. This handsomely styled and generously equipped EV features three rows of seats, all-wheel drive, and 402 horsepower. Its driving range, estimated by the EPA at 287 miles per charge, is roughly on par with other mid-size electric SUVs.

The cabin looks nice and features plenty of amenities, but we haven’t had a chance to take one for a test drive just yet. We have, however, driven its smaller sibling, the VF8 , and our initial impressions of that model were less than complimentary. If you’re in the mood to drive something unique and can stomach the potential risk of buying a vehicle from a start-up automaker, the VF9 is worth a test drive.
Expert Tip: If you need three rows but want more driving range, the Hyundai Ioniq 9 offers a similar form factor but can travel for up to 311 miles per charge.

VinFast’s flagship three-row SUV skipped the 2026 model year but has returned for 2027 with a new, lower price. The previous entry-level trim was the Eco, but that’s been jettisoned from the lineup—for now—leaving the Plus trim as the sole offering. In 2025, the Plus commanded an optimistic $75,190, but for 2027 it’s been reduced by $10,900 to $64,290. The base Eco trim could return to the lineup later on with an even lower price.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

The VF9 is all-wheel drive and uses two electric motors to generate 402 horsepower. We haven’t driven the VF9 yet, but we found the suspension of the smaller VF8 to be in need of some tuning. Whether that applies to the VF9, we will learn when we get behind the wheel. When we do, we'll report our findings here.

In Comparison: The VF9’s estimated 60 mph time puts it at a disadvantage when compared to other three-row electric SUVs we’ve tested. The Kia EV9 , for example, needed just 4.5 seconds to reach 60 mph in our testing.

It’s been a mainstay on our 10Best award list since it arrived in 2020, excelling for its ability to provide impressive performance at an attainable price. But for many enthusiasts, one thing remains missing: a manual transmission. Now, however, there’s at least one manual C8 Corvette, with Alex Peitz of Peitz Performance showing off his stick-shift Vette at this year’s SEMA show.

Last year at SEMA, transmission maker Tremec unveiled a manual transmission that it said was compatible with the C8 Corvette . The reveal proved somewhat controversial, with Corvette chief engineer Tony Roma later saying , “Tremec showed something at SEMA last year that I wish they wouldn’t have shown. It’s not real. So when people say, ‘But there’s one that’s available,’ there isn’t.”

Now a year later, Peitz is showing that the C8-ready Tremec TR-9060 six-speed manual transaxle certainly is real, and he’s become the first person to actually put it to use, at least publicly. Peitz had already 3-D scanned his Corvette in order to implement some track-day modifications, which certainly eased the process of fitting all of the new parts in, and given the car’s track-ready status, the final result is definitely still quite raw.

Still, Peitz has proved it’s possible, even if it took a bit of work to get everything to fit together. Peitz’s manual C8 uses a Porsche aftermarket gear selector and the clutch pedal from a CT4-V Blackwing , for which they built a custom bracket to mount it to the brake-pedal assembly before adding a pedal stop and hydraulic clutch assist. Peitz also snagged a flywheel from McLeod that uses the ring and teeth from a C8 flywheel and added a clutch.

Electronics are managed by a pair of MoTeC controllers: an M182 unit controls the engine, while an M150 unit handles ignition cuts when shifting with the manual transmission. Peitz Performance aims to start offering this plug-and-play setup to customers soon, which is designed to work with the manual or the factory dual-clutch transmission. The system still works with the factory wiring harness, as well as the standard instrument panel, ABS, and power-steering systems.

While this initial manual C8 is still a bit rough around the edges, Peitz aims to turn his one-off build into a conversion that customers can order using a single part number. Hot Rod got a chance to get behind the wheel of Peitz’s Vette and called the manual transmission “transformative.” Peitz has shown that the Tremec TR-9060 is real and can work, and we wouldn’t be shocked to see more manual-converted Corvettes at next year’s SEMA show.

Tesla desperately wants its FSD software approved in Europe, but so far it's only been adopted piecemeal. The latest adopter? Finland, which approved the tech with some slight modifications — but said that it may not vote the same way in an EU-wide decision. From Reuters :

STOCKHOLM, Nov 11 (Reuters) – Finland ‌granted provisional approval on Wednesday for Tesla's Assisted Driving system (TAD) after the US automaker made changes to the technology, allowing its use on Finnish roads ahead of an EU-wide ​vote.

Nearly a dozen countries, including Slovakia and Belgium, have granted provisional approvals for ​the technology, which allows vehicles to steer, accelerate and brake automatically ⁠under driver supervision.
However, Tesla has yet to secure backing from any of ​the EU's largest member states, whose support is likely to be crucial to ​winning approval across the bloc.
Finland's transport authority, Traficom, said it ​approved the system after Tesla renamed it from "Full Self-Driving" and tightened speed-control settings ​that critics said encouraged speeding.

FSD is, really, Tesla's flagship at the moment. The Roadster isn't real , the Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck are all dead, the Semi only sort of exists for fleet sales, and the Optimus robot will likely never be a household product. Tesla's big thing is its software, and it can't sell that software in a major economic bloc. Not a great look for a company that pretends not to be a car company — though at this point, with only two real offerings, maybe it's no longer pretending.

title: The Netherlands Has €231 Million for Cleaner Inland Ships. It Still Needs Electric Freight Corridors
raw_summary: The Netherlands is preparing to spend €231.2 million over four years helping inland ships replace fossil-fuel propulsion. The first €36.93 million tender opens on November 17, 2026, and battery-electric vessels are among the eligible investments. This is a serious step toward decarbonizing freight on the waterways that link Dutch ports and Europe's industrial heartland. But the programme's most important scoring calculation rewards emissions avoided per euro of propulsion subsidy while excluding separate subsidies for the shore infrastructure on which the ship may depend. That distinction matters when the commercial product is a complete freight service, not an electric vessel sitting beside a quay. The new Dutch tender is considerably more sophisticated than a technology demonstration fund, yet it leaves an important accounting boundary. My TFIE Strategy Briefing assessment follows that boundary from subsidized vessels to working routes, drawing on my open, 98-page Inland Freight Electrification report .

article_paragraphs: The Netherlands is preparing to spend €231.2 million over four years helping inland ships replace fossil-fuel propulsion. The first €36.93 million tender opens on November 17, 2026, and battery-electric vessels are among the eligible investments. This is a serious step toward decarbonizing freight on the waterways that link Dutch ports and Europe's industrial heartland. But the programme's most important scoring calculation rewards emissions avoided per euro of propulsion subsidy while excluding separate subsidies for the shore infrastructure on which the ship may depend. That distinction matters when the commercial product is a complete freight service, not an electric vessel sitting beside a quay.

The new Dutch tender is considerably more sophisticated than a technology demonstration fund, yet it leaves an important accounting boundary. My TFIE Strategy Briefing assessment follows that boundary from subsidized vessels to working routes, drawing on my open, 98-page Inland Freight Electrification report .

The RVO programme can support battery-electric systems, some hybrid arrangements and other propulsion technologies, together with eligible charging and refueling facilities. Its published explanation prioritizes electrification where practical. That is sensible: electric inland vessels are already operating in the Netherlands, and a subsidy should encourage the pathway that provides the required service at low emissions and acceptable cost.

The scheme also recognizes that a vessel does not operate in isolation. Applications receive points for commercial cooperation, cargo-owner agreements and the quality of supporting infrastructure arrangements. These are material criteria, not decorative promises. They are a welcome correction to programmes that fund novel equipment and assume the market, terminal and utility will somehow arrange everything else.

Yet most of the available points are tied to projected emissions reductions per euro of propulsion support. That is a consistent measure for comparing applications for individual ships. It is not an accounting of the entire investment required to turn a diesel freight route into an electric one. One barge may need access to battery exchange at both ends of its journey, reserve battery inventory, grid capacity, a crane or handling system and a dependable service agreement. Some of those facilities can serve many vessels, making it hard to allocate their cost and value to any single propulsion application.

Zero Emission Services, or ZES, has already shown what putting the pieces together looks like. Its swappable battery containers allow inland vessels to obtain charged energy without each owner purchasing and maintaining every battery required by the route. At Moerdijk, a terminal arrangement combines battery exchange, handling equipment and access to an existing electricity connection. The ZES network is extending beyond isolated demonstrations, although operating sites, planned stations and funded vessel conversions must not be counted as the same thing.

The difference between a capable ship and reliable freight is familiar to ports. Charged batteries must be available at the right time, terminals must handle exchanges without disrupting cargo work, and the energy-service provider needs enough committed traffic to finance its containers and chargers.

The Netherlands deserves credit for recognizing these dependencies. It need not discard vessel-level grants or wait until every future route is planned before making early awards. But a second programme-level measure is needed alongside emissions per propulsion subsidy: what complete, repeatable electric freight service is each funded project helping create, and which shared assets make that service possible?

If the idea of a low, powerful, sporty pickup truck akin to the new Ram Rumble Bee series or Roush's own street-focused F-150 Nitemare appeals to you, then this Roush F-150 might be right up your alley.

The truck uses a naturally aspirated 5.8-liter Windsor V8 with upgraded valve springs, aluminum rocker arms, aluminum heads, a custom intake, and a new exhaust. Roush's latest Mustang supercharger kit makes 810 hp, but there's no word on how much power this F-150's Windsor puts out. Perhaps more important than outright power is the fact that it has a five-speed manual transmission, a limited-slip differential, and sends its power exclusively to the rear wheels.

Roush built these pickups to promote its racing team and transformed their exterior. This one was refinished in an eye-catching white, blue, and red livery inspired by Mark Martin's No. 6 NASCAR Thunderbird and fitted with a Flareside bed conversion. The truck also sits on special 17-inch wheels with chunky 315/35 Goodyear tires. The firm has installed new springs and shocks to give it the low ride height. Beefed-up brakes have also been installed.

It'd ordinarily be difficult to place a value on a vehicle as rare as this. However, things are a little different here. This very truck was sold by Mecum Auctions just six weeks ago as part of its huge sale of Roush-branded vehicles. The truck ended up selling for $41,800, roughly double what Roush now charges to give a 2027 Ford Super Duty its off-road makeover , and the BaT seller will no doubt be hopeful they can flip it for more than that. Adding to the truck's appeal is that it shows just over 12,000 miles on the odometer.

The race-inspired upgrades extend beyond the engine and exterior. Found in the truck's cabin are special blue seats, a roll cage, Simpson racing harnesses, and a three-spoke steering wheel. Although this F-150 is all about the driving experience, it does retain some creature comforts, including a stereo system and air conditioning.

Roush used this special F-150 at events with former stock car racing driver Mark Martin and also displayed it at Valvoline oil shops. It also featured in the music video for Sammy Kershaw's "Anywhere but Here ."

article_paragraphs: Tesla’s “flying” Roadster just took a hit from Porsche. Speaking at a conference in Berlin today, CEO Michael Leiters said Porsche wants “to completely steer clear from any kind of effects and shows,” according to Bloomberg .

Both automakers revealed their next halo cars on the same day, October 15. Tesla made a Roadster flip in mid-air. Porsche showed the Mission S, and Leiters says the two cars aren’t even chasing the same customers.

Tesla finally unveiled the next-gen Roadster last month, almost nine years after the 2017 prototype. The main event was a car using compressed-air thrusters to launch off a ramp, rotate in the air, and come back down on its wheels.

It was the payoff for months of hype. Musk spent most of the year promising a “flying” Roadster demo, and it slipped more than once. We reported in June that it had been pushed to August to make room for SpaceX thruster work.

There are three versions. The Performance trim uses suction fans and claims 0-60 mph in under 1.6 seconds, the Thrust trim adds rear cold-gas thrusters for a claimed sub-0.9-second run, and the single-seat Rocket trim gets thrusters all around the car and isn’t approved for public roads. Tesla gave no price and no production date, just Musk’s “2028, actually.”

Porsche went the other way. Under the skin, the Mission S can take either a hybrid or a straight combustion powertrain. It’s a mid-engine car that sits above the 911 in the lineup, and well above it in price.

Leiters said customer response has been “overwhelming” and that Porsche would rather show off real technical innovation than put on a show. If it reaches production, Ferrari is the obvious target, and Porsche hasn’t played in that segment since the 918 Spyder. Porsche is counting on a pricier, more exclusive lineup to rebuild its profits.
Not everyone in the supercar world agrees with Leiters. Ferrari CEO Benedetto Vigna rated Tesla’s Roadster launch “10 out of 10” last month.

Different people find different things exciting, too, so it's not an objective measure, but it's an important factor in why people choose to buy a car in the first place. Whether you're in the market for a new car or not, we want to know, what new car excites you the most? Sound off in the comments section below to share your answer with your fellow Jalops.

For the most part, Americans are facing financial difficulties at the moment, from the raging affordability crisis to absurdly high fuel prices and a litany of other challenges, so maybe your view of an exciting car is one that's actually affordable for the average Joe. Maybe you love small cars so you're stoked on the Scion by Toyota KEI-01 , or you're a horsepower addict who is more excited about the C8 Corvette Grand Sport's new 6.7-liter V8 . There are no wrong answers, we just want to know what new car excites you the most.

The new car that excites me the most is the new Rivian R2 . It's no secret that the Tesla Model Y sells like hotcakes, but I find it encouraging to see that a different American automaker that's not run by the world's richest and most narcissistic man can also produce an appealing, affordable, and effective competitor. I love Rivian's design language, and I think the R2 is super cool and looks truly distinctive when compared to other compact SUVs.

A fully loaded R2 Performance AWD Launch Edition rings in at about $60,000. For that price you get a whopping 656 horsepower and 609 lb-ft of torque, which is good enough for 0-to-60 sprints of around 3.5 seconds while still providing around 330 miles of range. Plus, its rear window rolls down like a Toyota 4Runner, a fantastic feature that I think more cars should have.

I think it will provide a genuinely wonderful ownership experience for thousands of buyers, and maybe even spark the next generation of car enthusiasts, which is truly exciting. But that's enough from little old me, you're here for you and your fellow Jalopnik readers! Head down to the comments section and share which new car excites you the most.

raw_summary: Bajaj Auto has slapped its upgrade package on two more Pulsars. We’re talking about the new and upgraded Pulsar NS200 UG and the new and upgraded Pulsar N250 SS. Looking at just the spec-sheets, Pulsar NS200 UG still comes out as the more tempting option owing to its high-revving liquid-cooled engine and then the more premium perimeter frame along with sportier clip-on handlebar. Also, it costs just Rs 1,000 more than Pulsar N250 SS. However, experience in real world is what matters and that is what we tried to find out at the media rides in Pune.

Where colours are concerned, both these updated Pulsars still don’t get solid colours without graphics. Pulsar N250 SS gets four colours – Brooklyn Black, Pearl Metallic White, Fiery Red Orange and the Atlantic Blue. Only Black and Red get Red painted alloy wheels, while other two colours get Black wheels.

Shifting the gaze towards Pulsar NS200 UG, we have just three colours and none of them are solid colours and they all get graphics. These include Pearl Metallic White, Ebony Black Racing Red and then the new Nardo Grey. Except for the White colour, which gets Black wheels, the other two get Red painted alloy wheels.

Bajaj Auto has given both these bikes the same upgrade package. So, both of them get the same 5-inch TFT instrument cluster that supports auto brightness, lap timer, document storage, music control and even Google Maps mirroring, which is a cherry on top. This screen is bright and has auto theme switching – Day / Night.

To control this screen, we now get new left-side switchgear which we have seen with other Pulsars. Both Pulsar N250 SS and Pulsar NS200 UG get new right side switchgear too, where Bajaj has added a hazard light button, an integrated engine kill switch / engine starter. The bike now gets a panic brake alert too, which is welcome addition.

Upgrade package also involves adjustable clutch and brake levers along with Type-C port. Both bikes now get an electronic throttle body with ride by wire that has enabled Ride Modes. Traction Control with both bikes can be switched off from the screen and then they both get a bi-directional quickshifter too. ABS modes are present with both the bikes and they both get rear radial tyres now.

Apart from the same upgrade package with both Pulsar N250 SS and Pulsar NS200 UG , there are some unique upgrades to these bikes individually too. For example, the Pulsar NS200 UG now gets slightly fatter USD front forks – 37mm, as opposed to 33mm from before. Also, the 199.5cc engine is updated to produce 25 PS and 18.74 Nm. Peak power is up by 1 PS and corresponding RPMs are also slightly higher.

raw_title: At $17,000, Is This Meyers Manx SR2 A Super Cool Cat?
title: At $17,000, Is This Meyers Manx SR2 A Super Cool Cat?
raw_summary: Today's Nice Price or No Dice Manx SR2 is the second VW-based kit car offered by legendary builder Bruce Meyers, and it features a design he thought would be far harder to copy than his first: the ubiquitous dune buggy. Let's decide what such a unique bit of car culture should cost. With the recent discontinuation of the Supra, fans eager to carry the torch of non-tepid Toyotas are left with only the GR86 coupe and the crazily expensive GR Corolla as rides of choice. The fact that Toyota couldn't be bothered to develop the last-generation Supra on its own, leveraging BMW for most of the under-skirt bits, makes it questionable whether the company even has any interest in sporty cars anymore. Instead of pulse-pumping sports cars, the company offers around a dozen five-door crossover-style vehicles, since that's what sells these days.
summary: Today's Nice Price or No Dice Manx SR2 is the second VW-based kit car offered by legendary builder Bruce Meyers, and it features a design he thought would be far harder to copy than his first: the ubiquitous dune buggy. Let's decide what such a unique bit of car culture should cost.
article_paragraphs: Today's Nice Price or No Dice Manx SR2 is the second VW-based kit car offered by legendary builder Bruce Meyers, and it features a design he thought would be far harder to copy than his first: the ubiquitous dune buggy. Let's decide what such a unique bit of car culture should cost.

With the recent discontinuation of the Supra, fans eager to carry the torch of non-tepid Toyotas are left with only the GR86 coupe and the crazily expensive GR Corolla as rides of choice. The fact that Toyota couldn't be bothered to develop the last-generation Supra on its own, leveraging BMW for most of the under-skirt bits, makes it questionable whether the company even has any interest in sporty cars anymore. Instead of pulse-pumping sports cars, the company offers around a dozen five-door crossover-style vehicles, since that's what sells these days.

That wasn't always the case; in addition to the Supra, Toyota once offered a rally-bred version of the stalwart Celica and a full-blown mid-engine sports car in the MR2. We looked at a 1993 Toyota MR2 on Tuesday, a non-turbo car that otherwise had all the options we'd want. Unfortunately, that non-turbo nature and a non-working A/C compressor called into question its $14,000 asking price. In the end, you all gave that a heave-ho in an 85% 'No Dice' downvote.

A lack of taint-tightening Toyotas doesn't mean that the automotive landscape has totally turned into dullsville, however. There are plenty of fun and interesting cars and, yes, even trucks, out there from which to choose when something more than sleepwalking self-driving is in order. But what if you wanted something crazier than what's on the menu right now from the ever-shrinking cadre of entertaining cars on the market? That's when a rare opportunity like today's Meyers Manx SR feels especially apt.

The SR2's creator, Bruce Meyers, grew up living the California dream. A bohemian artist and engineer, Meyers spent his early adult years surfing, off-road racing, and teaching himself to mold fiberglass as a boat builder. His talents all merged in the creation of the original Meyers Manx dune buggy, introduced in 1964.

Built on a VW Type 1 platform shortened by 14.5 inches, the Manx immediately became an icon and set off an industry of copycats. Meyers went to court to stop the copiers from making dime on his design, but to little success. Taking another tack, Meyers' next street kit, the Manx SR2 (Street Roadster), was far more complex, featuring 10 body panels (as opposed to the original Manx's two) and iconic scissor-style doors. Unfortunately, the cost of the lawsuits, along with nasty letters from the IRS, ate away at Meyers' company finances, and he closed the doors in 1971. By that time, fewer than 200 Manx SR body kits had left the Fountain Valley factory.

This is one of those rare SR models, built on a VW Beetle platform, but powered by a Chevy Corvair air-cooled six. Unlike most automotive engines, the Corvair mill spins counterclockwise, so the car also has the Chevy four-speed manual gearbox instead of a VW transmission. According to the ad, the added power (likely around 140 horsepower gross) makes the car "fly!"

The car rolls, appropriately enough, on a set of Western Bullet Torque Thrust-style wheels wrapped in white-letter BF Goodrich tires. They sit proud in the exaggerated wheel arches, looking almost comically large in comparison to the car's miniature 80-inch wheelbase.

article_paragraphs: Following our report on India’s top 10 best-selling cars in October 2026 , we take a closer look at the country’s best-selling sedans during the month. Despite a continued shift in consumer preference towards SUVs and utility vehicles, the sedan segment delivered positive performance.

The top 10 sedans collectively recorded wholesale dispatches of 41,773 units in October 2026, compared to 37,211 units in the same month last year. This translates into a healthy year-on-year (YoY) growth of 12.3%, indicating that sedans continue to retain a significant share of the Indian passenger vehicle market.

Leading the segment was Maruti Suzuki Dzire, which continued its dominance as India’s best-selling sedan. However, sales witnessed a marginal 0.7% YoY decline, with 20,649 units dispatched in Oct 2026 as against 20,791 units in Oct 2025. Despite the slight dip, Dzire accounted for a commanding 49.4% share of top 10 sedan sales.

In a second spot was the Hyundai Aura with 7,349 unit sales in the past month. Sales improved by 26.4% YoY over 5,815 units of Oct 2025. The recently launched Tata Aeris commanded a third spot on this list with 4,005 unit sales. Honda Amaze continued to attract buyers, finishing fourth with 3,337 units. However, sales declined 8.1% YoY compared to the 3,630 units dispatched in Oct 2025.

Delivering strongest YoY performance was the Skoda Slavia. Sales improved by 60.1% to 2,638 units in the past month from 1,648 unit sales of the same month last year. This indicates growing customer interest for premium midsize sedans. Slavia overtook Volkswagen Virtus by 750 units.

VW Virtus, also in the premium midsize sedan category showed off contrasting performances. Virtus featured at No. 6 on this list and has suffered a steep 23% YoY decline in sales to 1,888 units from 2,453 units. VW is getting ready to launch the updated Virtus in coming weeks.

Hyundai Verna, in a seventh spot, accounted for 775 unit sales in the past month. Sales dipped 5.9% when compared to 824 units sold in Oct 2025. Honda City sales went up by 3.1% YoY to 596 units over 578 units sold in the same month last year.

At the lower end of the rankings, Tata Tigor witnessed a significant decline in demand. Sales plunged 72.1% YoY to just 334 units against 1,196 units in Oct 2025. Toyota Camry rounded off the list with 202 units, registering a 26.8% YoY decline compared to 276 units sold in the same month of last year.

title: Science For The People, Right On!
raw_summary: Today United for the Future launches at COP31 today with a plan to unite 100 million people in peaceful, non-partisan marches in cities worldwide. Their goal is to assemble the largest coordinated climate demonstration in history in order to put climate action back at the top of the political agenda. Backers of the initiative include Christiana Figueres, former UN climate chief and a key architect of the Paris Agreement; Bill McKibben, author and co-founder of 350.org; Ram Ramanathan of Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego; and Sandrine Dixson-Declève, honorary president of the Club of Rome.

article_paragraphs: Today United for the Future launches at COP31 today with a plan to unite 100 million people in peaceful, non-partisan marches in cities worldwide. Their goal is to assemble the largest coordinated climate demonstration in history in order to put climate action back at the top of the political agenda.

Backers of the initiative include Christiana Figueres, former UN climate chief and a key architect of the Paris Agreement; Bill McKibben, author and co-founder of 350.org; Ram Ramanathan of Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego; and Sandrine Dixson-Declève, honorary president of the Club of Rome.

Together, they beckon citizens around the world: “Protect our future. Act on the science.” Their call asks governments to stop weakening climate protections and to deliver action that cuts emissions and protects nature in line with science.

Limiting temperature rise to a 1.5 degrees Celsius, or 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit, above the preindustrial levels of the early 1800s was a goal established during the 2015 Paris Agreement. Since then, it’s been a focus of international climate negotiations, and one that’s often been politically contentious.

“For too many people, climate change is deadly,” UN climate chief Simon Stiell said at COP31. “At this COP, nations face a choice: electric or shock. Rewire the global economy for the electric age. Or accept ongoing fossil fuel cost pain for families, firms, and governments.”

Global carbon emissions from fossil fuels are projected to decrease by 0.4% in 2026, driven by expansion of solar and wind power and the Iran conflict, according to new research by the Global Carbon Project .

Then there’s the recent blue tsunami that took place in the US midterm elections, which served as a condemnation of the Trump administration. Historian and activist Rebecca Solnit exclaims, “It was a dam breaking, the dam that held back the will of the people, the people of the world’s most diverse country, the people who believed in their own rights and equality and in the rights and equality of others.”

Now, through promised agendas to increase affordability for consumers, Democrats have a keen opportunity to foreground science as a way to accomplish goals. Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT) admonishes the new Democratic majority to deliver on its campaign jargon. “No more empty rhetoric. No more telling us how terrible Trump and the Republicans are. No more excuses,” he says. “We now have the votes to pass legislation that will demonstrably improve the lives of millions of working families. And that’s what we must do.”

article_paragraphs: Honda's worrying return of reliability problems includes a new issue, the root cause of which it might not trace before the end of the Formula 1 season.
Aston Martin and engine partner Honda suffered their third DNF of the triple-header in Brazil, when Lance Stroll retired for the second race in a row.
Stroll had two separate battery problems over the course of the Brazil weekend and didn't make it to mid-distance in Sunday's grand prix.
It means Stroll has finished just six of the 20 races held this season, while team-mate Fernando Alonso has had seven retirements of his own.

There have been some flashes of optimism - in relative terms, given how disastrous this first season of the new alliance has been - of late as Alonso scored points in Malaysia five races ago, had surprisingly good pace at Austin despite sustaining significant floor damage on the opening lap , and excelled in the wet in Brazil.
There, Alonso comfortably gave Aston Martin and Honda their best qualifying of the year, getting into Q3 for the first time and lining up eighth on the grid.
But this has been badly undercut by a return of significant fragility that's closer to how badly Honda started 2026.

Reliability problems also put paid to Alonso's chances in Mexico, where he had looked quite competitive and closer to the top 10 than normal. The issue was related to the cooling system inside the energy recovery system, whereas in Brazil the emergence of battery problems for Stroll sounded a clear alarm bell.

raw_summary: Every few years, I apparently feel compelled to remind Honda that it is sitting on what could be one of the easiest home runs in the electric motorcycle industry: just make an electric Super Cub already. article_paragraphs: Every few years, I apparently feel compelled to remind Honda that it is sitting on what could be one of the easiest home runs in the electric motorcycle industry: just make an electric Super Cub already.

I’m not talking about an electric scooter vaguely inspired by the Super Cub. Not another futuristic concept with swoopy bodywork and a name that looks like a Wi-Fi password. I mean an actual honest-to-goodness Honda Super Cub, except electric.
The Honda Super Cub is arguably the most successful motor vehicle ever created, with well over 100 million produced since its introduction in 1958. It’s still in continuous production today.

And a huge part of that success comes down to how approachable the thing is. It isn’t supposed to be intimidating, excessively powerful, or particularly complicated. It’s simple, practical transportation wrapped in one of the most recognizable two-wheeler designs ever created.

The beauty of the bike is how simple and timeless it is, with the appearance barely changing in nearly 7 decades. And with the design freedom that electric drivetrains provide, upgrading the cute little bike to an electric future would be a walk in the park for Honda’s engineers.
An in-wheel motor would be a simple, cheap solution that frees up even more space in the body for batteries.

And Honda wouldn’t need some enormous battery capable of highway touring. Give an electric Super Cub enough battery for perhaps 50-60 miles (80-95 km) of real-world urban riding, a motor capable of roughly 50-60 mph (80-95 km/h), and simple Level 1 charging from a normal wall outlet. As a city runabout or a beachside cruiser, those middle-of-the-road specs would be perfect.

Even better, make the battery removable. Honda already has its Mobile Power Pack e: swappable battery system used in various electric two-wheelers, and an electric Super Cub would be an incredible platform to expand it.

title: What the Brazilian GP revealed about F1's ability to cope with rain
raw_summary: The question of what might happen in a wet race has vexed Formula 1's stakeholders since before the beginning of the season. It's also prompted some unnecessarily hysterical commentary throughout the year, peaking in the run-up to last weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos, where rain for qualifying and the race was a virtual certainty for the first time this season. This was not the case in Brazil.

article_paragraphs: The question of what might happen in a wet race has vexed Formula 1's stakeholders since before the beginning of the season. It's also prompted some unnecessarily hysterical commentary throughout the year, peaking in the run-up to last weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos, where rain for qualifying and the race was a virtual certainty for the first time this season.

Although the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was interrupted by rain and the discovery of a software glitch, by the time the race got going the track was drying quickly. This was not the case in Brazil.
Qualifying at Interlagos was red-flagged for 80 minutes after a downpour coincided with the start of the session, and many media outlets alighted on a spicy George Russell quote in the aftermath.

"I love driving in the rain here but, at some point, if that was a race, there was no way we should be driving in that because the chances of seeing a really, really horrific incident are very, very high," he said.

Perfect headline material for a noisy story, but context was lacking. The general consensus within the paddock after that session was that the FIA made the right calls at the right time, immediately suspending Q1 during the initial downpour, then applying great rigour to identify a safe ‘window' to restart it.

"In general, I want to race, but yesterday [Saturday] I think it was the perfect call," said Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur after the race. "When we did the first [Q1] lap before the red flag, we came back with two centimetres of water in the car…"

Those conditions were too wet to stage any kind of track activity beyond a boat race in the pitlane. The real questions surrounded how the cars and the latest generation of tyres would perform in the kind of wet and/or rapidly changing circumstances in which qualifying and the race could actually be staged.

Historically, Pirelli's heavily treaded ‘extreme' wet tyres are rarely seen, since too much of their operating window sits outside the margin of what is considered to be acceptable racing conditions. They displace massive quantities of water but the tread blocks overheat too quickly as the track dries. By the time the track is wet enough to justify the ‘extreme' tyre, a red flag is usually imminent.

It's also prompted some unnecessarily hysterical commentary throughout the year, peaking in the run-up to last weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos, where rain for qualifying and the race was a virtual certainty for the first time this season.

title: India-Made Renault Kiger Improves Safety Rating
raw_summary: In 2022, Global NCAP tested the Renault Kiger (pre-facelift model) under their Safer Cars for Africa campaign. This compact SUV scored 2 Stars in that test and the model that was subjected to the crash tests was equipped with 2 airbags as standard and without ESC and ISOFIX child seat mounts. Now that Renault Kiger has been updated with a facelift and improved equipment list, it was subjected to Global NCAP crash tests again. article_paragraphs: In 2022, Global NCAP tested the Renault Kiger (pre-facelift model) under their Safer Cars for Africa campaign. This compact SUV scored 2 Stars in that test and the model that was subjected to the crash tests was equipped with 2 airbags as standard and without ESC and ISOFIX child seat mounts.

Now that Renault Kiger has been updated with a facelift and improved equipment list, it was subjected to Global NCAP crash tests again. Global NCAP has just published the results of new Renault Kiger and it scored 4 Stars for adult occupant protection and 3 Stars for child occupant protection, marking a major improvement in safety.

Made in India Renault Kiger has just undergone the rigorous Global NCAP crash testing process and has massively upped the safety quotient from previous 2 Stars to now scoring 4 Stars. This particular Kiger is the newer facelifted model launched in India in August 2026 and it is manufactured at their Chennai plant and shipped to 16 countries globally.

In the latest crash tests, the Renault Kiger unit subjected to crash tests had 6 airbags, ISOFIX child seat mounts, ESC, seatbelt reminders, seatbelt pretensioners and load limiters. The updated Renault Kiger scored 25.20 / 34 points in adult occupant protection and 30.21 / 49 points in child occupant protection.

As per Global NCAP assessment in the frontal test, footwell area and bodyshell were rated unstable and unable to withstand further loadings. Head of three-year-old dummy contacted the vehicle interior and the chest showed high decelerations. In the side impact test, one door opened during the test, resulting in a point deduction. Head, abdomen and pelvis protection were good and chest protection was adequate.

Head exposure brought all of the three-year-old’s side impact points to zero. The 18-month-old dummy showed full protection in both the frontal and side impact tests. In the side pole impact test, head and pelvis protection were good, abdomen protection was adequate and chest protection was marginal. The car met pedestrian protection regulation UN127 and complied with Global NCAP’s ESC and seatbelt reminder (SBR) requirements.

Richard Woods, Chief Executive Officer, Global NCAP, said “It’s satisfying to see the safety improvements Renault has introduced with the updated Kiger in South Africa. We welcome their positive engagement and hope that this approach now becomes a trend across the industry. It demonstrates what can be achieved when a manufacturer seeks to prioritise safety, and it shows why six airbags must become a standard requirement.”

article_paragraphs: Proposed Rule Would Shut the Public Out and Allow the Administration to Make Sweeping Decisions About 250 Million Acres of Western Public Lands Behind Closed Doors

Yesterday, the Administration announced a proposed Bureau of Land Management (BLM) rulemaking that would drastically weaken the public’s involvement in land use planning and gut protections for Areas of Critical Environmental Concern (ACECs), one of BLM’s primary conservation designations, across 245 million acres of Western public lands. The rule proposes to stifle the voices of local communities by significantly shortening public comment periods and cutting out robust environmental analysis. These changes would make it easier for the BLM to fast-track the sale, transfer, or use of public lands for oil and gas drilling, mining, data centers, and other industrial or commercial development, all while shutting out the American people. The announcement kicks off a 60 day comment period (January 9th deadline).

The public lands overseen by the BLM contain crucial wildlife corridors, critical habitat, cultural resources and landscapes, watersheds, historic sites, and access to nature and scenery. The rule threatens to strip vital safeguards for ACECs and environmental review that protect these values, leaving the West’s most sensitive lands vulnerable to irreparable harm.

This aggressive regulatory rollback is the latest chapter in a coordinated, systematic dismantling of America’s public lands. It directly connects to a broader pattern of hostility toward balanced stewardship, which includes the recent rescission of the landmark Public Lands Rule, stated intention to roll back the Roadless Rule and Wilderness policies, the evisceration of National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) standards, and repeated attempts to give away public lands to corporations and developers. This rulemaking contributes to this administration’s singular focus: fast-tracking industrial exploitation and drilling at the expense of our shared heritage, tribal sovereignty and the outdoor recreation economies that sustain rural Western communities.
The proposal comes as Congress debates permitting legislation that would also weaken public participation in decisions affecting shared lands and give more power to development interests.

Planning serves as the foundational blueprints governing public lands for decades; eroding these processes is a profound threat to the long-term health of the West. Making robust environmental review optional and weakening ACEC standards intentionally ties the agency’s hands, preventing it from effectively responding to the compounding threats of climate change, drought, and habitat fragmentation. This action rejects the unmistakable demand from the American public, including local leaders, Tribal representatives, and local elected officials, who have consistently called for public lands to be managed transparently and protected for future generations.

“The Trump Administration is once again plotting to undermine our world-renowned system of shared lands and the public processes that guide their management,” said Jackie Feinberg, Sierra Club’s National Lands Conservation Manager . “Weakening protections and public participation would fast-track the industrialization and privatization of places essential for wildlife, clean water, cultural and historic preservation, and access to nature. We stand firmly against these attempts to cut out the “public” from public lands for the benefit of corporate polluters and profiteers.”

“Gutting transparency, review, and public engagement requirements within the West’s most ecologically sensitive wildlife corridors, watersheds, and cultural resources are the actions of cowards trying to fast-track industrial development at any and all social costs,” said Kara Matsumoto, senior policy director at the Conservation Lands Foundation . “Resource management plans are the blueprints for keeping public lands and waters healthy, and weakening them will weaken local economies and fragile ecosystems. We’ll continue to fight this corporate greed because the overwhelming majority of Americans want more nature protected, not less.”

raw_title: DOJ Slaps Lyft With $53 Million Lawsuit For Allegedly Discriminating Against Disabled Riders
title: DOJ Slaps Lyft With $53 Million Lawsuit For Allegedly Discriminating Against Disabled Riders
raw_summary: The U.S. Department of Justice is suing ride-hailing company Lyft , accusing it of routinely discriminating against people with disabilities in direct violation of federal law. The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, alleges that Lyft and its drivers "routinely refuse to serve" people with disabilities, such as folks who use stowable wheelchairs or ride with service animals. The DOJ also accused the San Francisco–based company of imposing cancellation fees on people who were denied service and charging passengers with disabilities higher fees and unnecessary surcharges. The Justice Department sought $53 million in damages for the "hundreds, and likely thousands" of customers it said Lyft and its drivers had wronged, and it's the latest in a series of legal actions the government has taken against major ride-hailing companies related to alleged Americans with Disabilities Act violations, according to Reuters . Just last year, the DOJ accused Uber of similar behavior and sought $125 million in damages. Uber says it has since committed to expanding access and improving the experience of riders with disabilities .

article_paragraphs: The U.S. Department of Justice is suing ride-hailing company Lyft , accusing it of routinely discriminating against people with disabilities in direct violation of federal law. The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California, alleges that Lyft and its drivers "routinely refuse to serve" people with disabilities, such as folks who use stowable wheelchairs or ride with service animals. The DOJ also accused the San Francisco–based company of imposing cancellation fees on people who were denied service and charging passengers with disabilities higher fees and unnecessary surcharges.

The Justice Department sought $53 million in damages for the "hundreds, and likely thousands" of customers it said Lyft and its drivers had wronged, and it's the latest in a series of legal actions the government has taken against major ride-hailing companies related to alleged Americans with Disabilities Act violations, according to Reuters . Just last year, the DOJ accused Uber of similar behavior and sought $125 million in damages. Uber says it has since committed to expanding access and improving the experience of riders with disabilities .

The department said Lyft failed to change its policies and practices to prevent this sort of discrimination, and it failed to adequately train drivers and customer service representatives about their obligations under federal law, The New York Times reports. On top of the $53 million in damages for passengers, the government is asking the court to consider a civil penalty against Lyft .
Uber, and now Lyft, have disagreed with the allegations vehemently. Here's what Lyft told The Times in a statement:

Discrimination has no place in the Lyft community. We have longstanding policies requiring drivers to accommodate riders who travel with service animals or use foldable mobility devices, and drivers who violate these policies face serious consequences, including permanent deactivation.
It should be noted that Lyft says it is fully cooperating with the Department of Justice through this entire process.

Unfortunately for everyone involved, this is not the first time Lyft has been in hot water over discriminating against folks with disabilities. As The Times points out, the company resolved allegations that its drivers denied services to people who used wheelchairs or walkers in 2020. Admittedly, the scope and penalties were far smaller back then, but it's a big deal nonetheless. Six years ago, it agreed to revise its policies and pay four passengers thousands of dollars in damages, along with a $40,000 civil penalty.

For example, this wing-style door can come in handy when parking the car in tight spaces. Since the door opens largely upwards, the side space requirement will be limited. The door is quite large, relative to the size of the micro car. This will allow easy ingress and egress for all passengers. In a parked scenario, the wing-style door can also provide clear views of the outside world.

Considering the car’s compact footprint, such features will also help avoid a sense of claustrophobia that some users might experience. Hero calls the NEX 3 a micro SUV, and its exterior styling backs up that claim. At the front, NEX 3 has a V-shaped grille structure. Lighting elements appear to be vertically stacked in a trapezoidal format, flanking the grille.

A full-width LED strip is expected on the bonnet. The micro car is using large aero-optimized alloy wheels, paired with low-profile tyres. Other key features include flared wheel arches, a large window for the second-row passenger and a gently sloping roofline. At the rear, Vida NEX 3 has a distinctive hexagonal-style boot lid and a prominent bumper.

Hero Vida NEX 3 is a 2-seater vehicle, designed primarily for swift mobility in modern cities. Interiors are largely minimalist, although some exciting colours have been used to perk up the cabin ambience. The micro car has a hexagonal-shaped steering wheel and a clutter-free dashboard with dual circular instrument dials.

Vida NEX 3 will have a customizable interior, allowing more personalization options to users. Even with its compact profile, the micro car has comfortable seating for two. While specifications for Vida NEX 3 have not been revealed, it is expected to get features like automatic AC and turn-by-turn navigation.

Though the design patent for Hero Vida NEX 3 has been filed, a specific launch timeline has not been revealed. Combining the convenience of a car and the compact profile of a two-wheeler, NEX 3 has potential to target a niche segment of buyers.
