KTM X-BOW has traditionally relied on powertrain partnerships with reputed manufacturers . This allows the brand to focus more on the engineering and performance aspects of the vehicle. For the all-new Arrow, an Audi-sourced 2.0-litre turbo petrol engine has been used. The standard model generates 280 hp, whereas the limited edition model is tuned to deliver 330 hp with the same engine.

The engine is paired with a 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox with a low range system. Both variants have selectable 2WD/4WD with locking front differential and limited-slip differential on the front axle. The limited edition model also has a limited-slip differential on the rear axle with disconnect system for fly-off handbrake. The standard model has a spool differential on the rear axle. Both variants have electronic power steering (EPS). The standard model has 3 drive modes, whereas the limited edition model has 4 drive modes.

KTM X-BOW Arrow has a dual-wishbone (A-arm) suspension with an anti-roll bar system at the front and rear. All wheels offer a massive 600 mm of suspension travel, allowing the vehicle to navigate demanding off-road terrain with ease. Front and rear shocks have manually adjustable dampers with the standard variant, whereas these are electrically adjustable on the limited edition model. The pricier model also benefits from performance brakes, as compared to standard brakes used with the base model.

While both versions have a welded tubular steel frame chassis, the limited edition model gets a fully closed cabin with carbon body outerwork. The standard model weighs 999 kg, whereas the limited edition model is heavier at 1,100 kg. Other parameters such as wheelbase (2,900 mm), ground clearance (430 mm), rack capacity (100 kg), storage capacity (100 litre) and fuel capacity (55 litre) are the same for both versions.

Both versions of X-BOW Arrow have a 10-inch centre display and driver display. With the standard model, key features include two USB C charging ports, rearview camera, GPS, group ride connectivity, sound system and speed limiter. The limited edition model gets additional features such as wiper and suspension adjustment, premium audio system and roof switch panel.

Common features include wearable RFID tag, premium high-performance LED headlights and aluminium protection at the front, middle and rear. The limited edition model has additional features such as 6 LEDs on the roof and a front mounted winch. The winch is removable and can be mounted at the rear as well.

The Dodge Viper was originally conceived as a modern version of the Shelby Cobra. This may seem odd given that the Cobra had been based on a Ford drivetrain, but Carroll Shelby had been hired by Chrysler in 1978 specifically to help resurrect the performance image of Dodge.

The man who had hired Shelby to work with Chrysler was the same man who had hired him to work with Ford, the great Lee Iacocca. Iacocca and Shelby had worked together on the Shelby Cobra , Ford GT40 , and Shelby Mustang programs – delivering a black eye to Ferrari with the dominant performances of the GT40 at the 24 Hours of Le Mans, winning the event four times on the trot from 1966 to 1969.

Once working on contract with Chrysler, Shelby and his team set to work creating a series of Dodge production cars with a series of performance upgrades. This was right in the midst of the Malaise Era, so these cars weren’t fast by today’s standards, but when viewed in the context of their time there were some genuinely quick Shelby-badged Dodges being built.

It would be in the middle of the 1980s that the idea of working with Shelby to develop a modern Shelby Cobra, within the Dodge family of course. The project was largely undertaken within Dodge, though Carroll Shebly did have input and would even drive a pre-production Viper as the pace vehicle in the Indianapolis 500 in 1991.

The Viper V10 was developed to one-up the V8 sitting in the engine bay of the Corvette – the Viper’s key competitor. It was an unusual all-alloy pushrod V10 with two valves per cylinder, and it caused an absolute sensation in the motoring media when it debuted.

title: Tesla tuner Unplugged offers to take over Cybertruck production
raw_summary: Unplugged Performance, the biggest name in Tesla aftermarket tuning, wants to keep the Cybertruck alive. The company publicly offered on Tuesday to take the Cybertruck line off Tesla’s hands, funded by a consortium of investors. It comes just four days after Elon Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027, with the truck selling at roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year Tesla planned for.

article_paragraphs: Unplugged Performance, the biggest name in Tesla aftermarket tuning, wants to keep the Cybertruck alive. The company publicly offered on Tuesday to take the Cybertruck line off Tesla’s hands, funded by a consortium of investors.

It comes just four days after Elon Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027, with the truck selling at roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year Tesla planned for.

UP posted the pitch on X as “an open offer to Tesla.” The company says it fully supports putting Cybercab first and would run Cybertruck production “at no cost to Tesla’s floor space, headcount, or focus.”

In exchange, Tesla would collect a license fee plus FSD and Robotaxi network revenue on every vehicle built. UP even offered to let Cybercab get first call on battery cells. “We’ll wait our turn,” the company wrote.
UP founder Ben Schaffer made it clear that he supports Tesla’s all-in move to autonomy, but he wants to keep the Cybertruck program alive.

And it isn’t stopping at the pickup. UP says it would build the Cybertruck, a three-row “CyberSUV,” and an unmanned “CyberCargo” hauler. Two vehicles Tesla has sometimes referenced, but they were never unveiled.

The post passed 240,000 views within hours, and the replies are mostly Cybertruck owners and Tesla shareholders begging Musk to say yes. Neither Musk nor Tesla had publicly responded at the time of writing.

UP has a lot riding on this. It sells an entire Cybertruck product line, the UP Invincible lift and armor kits, and it has scored several contracts to turn Cybertrucks into police vehicles for law enforcement agencies. CEO Ben Schaffer once described the company’s purpose as doing “the things that Tesla maybe wants to do, but doesn’t have the bandwidth to do.” This is that idea taken to its extreme.

New SEIA analysis shows that BAAJA could unlock 167 gigawatts of additional solar capacity between 2028 and 2035, bringing solar to over 18% of U.S. electricity generation by 2035. The analysis finds that the bill’s reforms could reduce cumulative power sector CO2 emissions by approximately 20% and avoid $54 billion in public health damages.

Founded in 1974, SEIA is the national trade association for the solar and solar + storage industries, building a comprehensive vision for the Solar+ Decade through research, education and advocacy. title: Introducing the Waymo Accessibility Network UK: Co-Designing the Future of Autonomous Mobility
raw_summary: Today, we’re launching the Waymo Accessibility Network UK to inform the future of autonomous mobility in the UK and enable a more independent future of transport. Whether it’s travelling to work, visiting friends, attending an appointment or simply enjoying everything a place has to offer, everyone deserves the freedom to travel with confidence and independence. Getting around should be about possibility, not barriers, and fully autonomous driving technology can provide more people with independent means of travel. “Establishing the Waymo Accessibility Network UK is a vital step in ensuring our rollout of autonomous technology in London is inclusive, equitable, and aligned with local needs,” says Chris Ludwick, Waymo Product Management Director . “Working hand-in-hand with our UK partners allows us to refine, test, and deploy solutions that give passengers the freedom of truly independent travel.”

“Establishing the Waymo Accessibility Network UK is a vital step in ensuring our rollout of autonomous technology in London is inclusive, equitable, and aligned with local needs,” says Chris Ludwick, Waymo Product Management Director . “Working hand-in-hand with our UK partners allows us to refine, test, and deploy solutions that give passengers the freedom of truly independent travel.”

Waymo’s Accessibility Network provides a forum for leading British disability advocates and charities to engage with our team in a consistent, two-way dialogue, ensuring that diverse voices within the UK’s disability community actively shape how our technology is deployed on UK streets. Waymo’s Accessibility Network UK is an extension of our longstanding commitment to inclusive mobility and how we continuously improve our service based on feedback from the disability community. That feedback lives within our product today, helping inform features like audio cues and vehicle-finding tools.

Robin Spinks, Head of Inclusive Design at the Royal National Institute of Blind People (RNIB) says: “RNIB warmly welcomes the Waymo Accessibility Network, and we look forward to contributing alongside the blind and partially sighted community.”

London is a global leader in transport. But as we have been hearing from UK accessibility groups over many years, getting around can still present daily challenges, in particular for disabled and older passengers. For sight impaired Londoners commuting at peak times, finding the right vehicle on a busy street can be difficult. Guide dog users still face refusals in private hire vehicles . For older passengers and people with different physical or cognitive needs, even seemingly small aspects of a journey can make a significant difference. As we shared in our Vision for London , opening travel to all matters – and autonomous driving technology offers the opportunity to rethink some of these experiences.

The Waymo Accessibility Network will work directly with member organisations to support user research and participate in product testing. The feedback from members helps inform the passenger experience of our fleet and build upon Waymo’s current accessible design features , including:

We are honoured to collaborate with an exceptional group of national and community-based organisations that champion inclusion across physical, sensory, and cognitive disabilities. We welcome our 10 inaugural participants: RNIB , Re-Engage , AgeUK , Transport for All , Thomas Pocklington Trust , Guide Dogs UK , Sense , Motability Foundation , National Centre for Accessible Transport and Scope .

“Autonomous technology offers enormous potential to transform independent travel, but it must be shaped by disabled people from day one. By joining the Waymo Accessibility Network UK, NCAT hopes to ensure that disability-centred design sits right at the heart of the UK’s autonomous vehicle future.” says Clive Gilbert, Consortium Board Member at the National Centre for Accessible Transport and Head of Accessible Transport at Policy Connect.

raw_title: A Trip Through Toyota’s New GR Garage Experience Center
title: A Trip Through Toyota's New GR Garage Experience Center
raw_summary: Toyota’s motorsports resume is a lot longer than you might expect. Long before Gazoo Racing was stamping GR badges onto Corollas , Supras , and the occasional RAV4 , Toyota was racing across the Australian Outback, battling American muscle cars in IMSA, and building some of the most successful prototype racers ever to cross the finish line. Near the Toyota Experience Center in Plano, Texas, the automaker has gathered an impressive collection of vehicles from its racing past. There’s a little bit of everything here: a 1957 Toyopet Crown that helped launch Toyota’s international racing ambitions, a legendary desert-racing pickup, a Le Mans prototype packing 1000 horsepower, and even a few cars from more recent spec series.
summary: Toyota’s motorsports resume is a lot longer than you might expect. Long before Gazoo Racing was stamping GR badges onto Corollas , Supras , and the occasional RAV4 , Toyota was racing across the Australian Outback, battling American muscle cars in IMSA, and building some of the most successful prototype racers ever to cross the finish line.
article_paragraphs: Toyota’s motorsports resume is a lot longer than you might expect. Long before Gazoo Racing was stamping GR badges onto Corollas , Supras , and the occasional RAV4 , Toyota was racing across the Australian Outback, battling American muscle cars in IMSA, and building some of the most successful prototype racers ever to cross the finish line.

Near the Toyota Experience Center in Plano, Texas, the automaker has gathered an impressive collection of vehicles from its racing past. There’s a little bit of everything here: a 1957 Toyopet Crown that helped launch Toyota’s international racing ambitions, a legendary desert-racing pickup, a Le Mans prototype packing 1000 horsepower, and even a few cars from more recent spec series.
Here’s a look at some of the machines that helped build Toyota’s motorsports legacy at the new GR Garage Experience Center.

From the moment you walk into Toyota’s GR Experience Center, it’s obvious nearly every inch of this place has been curated to celebrate the brand’s motorsports history. Racing memorabilia, suspension components, and die-cast cars decorate the walls and many office rooms at the unassuming facility. It’s equal parts museum and shrine that honors the Japanese company’s obsession with racing.

Toyota’s international motorsports career began not with a World Rally car, but with this. In 1957, a Toyopet Crown entered the Mobilgas Round Australia Rally, an extraordinarily demanding endurance event covering thousands of miles of Australia's unforgiving landscape. The Crown finished 47th overall and third among foreign entries. They didn’t take home the trophy for first place, but surviving the 19-day endurance trial was plenty to brag about. More importantly, the experience exposed weaknesses Toyota would address in future vehicles.

Long before the Supra, there was the 2000GT. Toyota enlisted legendary American racer and car builder Carroll Shelby to develop the beautiful sports car for SCCA competition in 1968. Only three were prepared for the program, with Scooter Patrick driving the No. 33 car pictured here. The 2000GT’s 2.0-liter inline-six produced roughly 200 horsepower in racing trim, and the Shelby-prepared Toyotas proved surprisingly competitive against Porsche. Patrick finished second in the C-Production championship standings.

Don’t let the Celica badge fool you. This is about as closely related to a production Celica as a NASCAR stock car is to the sedan it resembles. Developed by Dan Gurney’s All American Racers, the IMSA GTO Celica used a tube-frame chassis, rear-wheel drive, and a heavily turbocharged inline-four engine producing as much as 600 horsepower. In 1987, Chris Cord and Toyota captured the IMSA GTO drivers’ and manufacturers’ championships. Not bad for a highly dramatized economy car.

Few vehicles are more immediately recognizable in off-road racing than Ivan “Ironman” Stewart’s red-and-white Toyota trucks. Built by Precision Preparation Inc. (PPI), these machines helped Stewart become one of the most successful drivers in desert racing history. Across his career, Stewart accumulated 84 victories and 10 championships, including 17 Baja 500 wins and three Baja 1000 victories. His nickname came from his willingness to tackle grueling desert events without a co-driver. Just imagine spending hundreds of miles bouncing around inside this thing. Sadly, most of us have only driven one of these via the Ironman “Ivan” Offroad Racing arcade game.

raw_title: Formula 2030 Concept Hints At Next Polestar 2
title: Formula 2030 Concept Hints At Next Polestar 2
raw_summary: Polestar got itself a new design boss in 2024, but it's taken a while for us to see what he's capable of. And if this new Formula 2030 concept is anything to go by, he was definitely the right man for the job. Philipp Römers' first show car for the EV brand is a sporty electric hatchback that Polestar says drops clues about how its next generation of production cars, including the new 2, will look. At 4,680 mm (184.3 inches) long, the Formula 2030 is shorter than a new 2027 BMW 3 Series , but wider than a Polestar 5 GT, and even lower. There's definitely a hint of Hyundai Ioniq 5 about the squat proportions, though to our eyes the Polestar's narrow glasshouse makes it look meaner.

article_paragraphs: Polestar got itself a new design boss in 2024, but it's taken a while for us to see what he's capable of. And if this new Formula 2030 concept is anything to go by, he was definitely the right man for the job. Philipp Römers' first show car for the EV brand is a sporty electric hatchback that Polestar says drops clues about how its next generation of production cars, including the new 2, will look.

At 4,680 mm (184.3 inches) long, the Formula 2030 is shorter than a new 2027 BMW 3 Series , but wider than a Polestar 5 GT, and even lower. There's definitely a hint of Hyundai Ioniq 5 about the squat proportions, though to our eyes the Polestar's narrow glasshouse makes it look meaner.

The clamshell hood with its deep center depression looks long by EV standards, and a pair of DRLs encase slim LED headlights. Polestar says we'll see those same Dual Blade headlights on the upcoming 2 crossover sedan. But probably not the vertical single windshield wiper, which looks like it escaped from an endurance racer. Just above the wiper's tip is a concealed Lidar sensor that pops out of the roof when the driver wants the car to share — or just take over — driving duties.

Swollen arches are filled with 22-inch center-lock wheels, and the rear doors hinge from the back, revealing the absence of a B-pillar. That's a common feature on concept cars, though one that rarely makes it to production. But one thing we'd like to see productionized is the rear hatch. The entire back end of the car lifts upwards, akin to a Group B rally mutant like the Lancia Delta S4 or Peugeot 205 T16 , to reveal a transparent trunk floor showcasing the Öhlins dampers.

Also notable at the back are the lights. Römers has junked the rear light bar that's a common theme on all of Polestar's current models in one form or another. Instead, the Formula 2030 has a slim LED blade on each side, which is probably a hint about how Polestar's next cars will look from the rear. It's funny how things come around. A few years ago, automakers were fitting full-width light bars so their cars would stand out, and now they're having to revert to regular lights to achieve the same effect.

A curved 20-inch gauge cluster mounted behind a yoke-style steering wheel sets the high-tech interior tone, but they're not the most interesting cabin details. That would be the 12.2-inch console touchscreen, which moves depending on what driving mode you've selected. Choose performance mode and the screen drops away into the console, while the steering wheel moves towards your chest so you can concentrate on the drive. But select autonomous mode and the wheel moves away, and the screen rises from the console to offer more infotainment services.

One surprise amid all of this tech is the presence of real switches. Polestar says owners can choose between rocker switches and rotary dials, and customize the functions of each. The automaker doesn't mention the powertrain, but it's a given that it's electric as the brand is fully committed to the EV cause. Unfortunately, however, Polestar can no longer commit to selling cars in America. It was forced to exit the U.S. after the 2026 model year due to restrictions on its Chinese software, meaning the bright new future the Formula 2030 points to will have to manage without access to the world's second biggest car market.

raw_summary: Kia opened orders for two new PV5 electric van variants, the PV5 Chassis and PV5 Cargo L2/H2, in the UK. The PV5 is Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business. article_paragraphs: Kia opened orders for two new PV5 electric van variants, the PV5 Chassis and PV5 Cargo L2/H2, in the UK.

The PV5 is Kia’s first fully electric van from its Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV) business. Built on Hyundai Motor’s dedicated modular skateboard platform, E-GMP.S, Kia can easily swap body styles to enable “limitless possibilities.”
So far, the PV5 has mostly been available in Passenger and Cargo body styles with several different variations.

Kia added the PV5 Chassis , an open-bed model that can be converted into just about anything. In the UK, Kia is offering conversions through TGS Automotive Group, including lightweight tipper, Dropside, and Box solutions.
The PV5 Chassis is available exclusively with the long-range 71.2 kWh battery in the UK , which Kia said could offer a potential WLTP range of up to 258 miles (416 km).
For reference, the PV5 Cargo L2/H1, which uses the same 71.2 kWh battery, offers a WLTP range of up to 258 miles (416 km). Other markets will also have a standard-range 51.1 kWh option.
The Chassis model is 4,610 mm long, 1,895 mm wide, and 1,935 mm tall, with a 2,995 mm wheelbase.
Its compact size and 5.5-meter turning radius, Kia said, make it easy to maneuver in city streets, construction sites, and other tight work areas.

raw_title: NASA Pushes Further Ahead With The Non-Space Side Of Its Mission, Teases New Experimental Plane
title: NASA Pushes Further Ahead With The Non-Space Side Of Its Mission, Teases New Experimental Plane
raw_summary: NASA has unveiled, sort of, its newest experimental plane. And by that, the agency appears to mean a plane meant to conduct experiments, rather than the plane itself being the experiment. Called the X-70 Fractal, the aircraft's primary selling point is its modular design, both inside and out. This means that payloads can be swapped out easily, whether they are hanging off the wings or nestled inside the plane. Even the flight controls can be reconfigured in case the agency wants to test different ways for the pilots (and it is piloted) to maneuver. The X-70 is really a platform to allow for a wide array of experiments on a single airframe, rather than creating a bespoke airframe to conduct one mission, like the X-59 is doing now . As for the plane itself, the X-70 Fractal is... well, more announcement than vehicle, at least for now. NASA says that it can carry 2,000 pounds of science equipment and take off with up to 10,000 pounds total. It will fly up to 45,000 feet in altitude, far above most airliners and well into the stratosphere. It will go up to 1,500 nautical miles, broadly on par with an F-35 . It also looks like an F-35, I think, maybe? For images, all we've got is this misty photo that looks AI generated. NASA seems to want to copy the energy of the F-47 and F/A-XX reveals , which are also foggy renderings and not actual photographs. Show me you're making an airplane without showing me you're making an airplane, I guess.

NASA seems to want to copy the energy of the F-47 and F/A-XX reveals , which are also foggy renderings and not actual photographs. Show me you're making an airplane without showing me you're making an airplane, I guess.

NASA achieves such historic feats in space that it's easy to forget that it is also an "Aeronautics" administration. Part of its remit is to push forward the boundaries of aviation here on this planet, which NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman has renewed focus on. Isaacman himself is a pilot who owns his own MiG-29 Soviet fighter jet , so this is an area of personal interest for him. In fact, he's promising that more experimental aircraft are on their way; rumors abound that the agency may be returning the famous SR-71 Blackbird, the fastest plane ever made, to service.

By doing so, NASA does important R&D on airplane technology that is then released into the public record, to the benefit of all aviation companies and everyone who flies on their products. That's the whole point of the X-59, which is trying to reduce the impact of sonic booms enough to make commercial supersonic planes financially viable. In addition, NASA's latest budget points to aviation as an area of strategic competition, per Wired . To that end, it may do some research alongside the Pentagon as well. This is where something like the X-70 is useful: it could do scientific, commercial, or military research as needed, simply by swapping out equipment payloads via its modular design. Now all NASA needs to do is, you know, build it, possibly with a contractor. Details!

article_paragraphs: No one likes greasy fingers, especially when they might cause a power-adjustable seat to move on its own. That’s the issue plaguing nearly 37,000 Lincoln Navigators, which are being recalled because their front passenger seat may unexpectedly move.

The recall involves 2025–2027 Navigator models with the “Chauffeur Seat Feature.” This function allows people sitting in the second row to control the front passenger seat’s movements via a touchscreen that’s built into the center console.

Based on the recall documents that Lincoln submitted to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), residue on the touch-activated display may cause the front passenger seat to unexpectedly move forward or back or recline up or down. Plus, if the home screen button is pressed on the rear touchscreen at the same time as a seat adjustment, Lincoln says this may cause the seat to move all the way to the end of its track without any buttons being pressed again.

While an empty seat that moves on its own is mostly just spooky, an occupied one could potentially cause an injury. That’s why Lincoln is asking owners to bring their affected Navigators to an authorized dealer so that the Chauffeur Seat Feature can be deactivated. This will be done for free, but it doesn’t sound like that function will work anymore. Finally, Lincoln says that both dealers and owners should have been notified by mail by now. If you haven’t received a letter and want to know if your SUV is part of the recall, you can use this feature on the NHTSA website to look up your VIN or search by year, make, and model, which will also show any other recall-related alerts.

Eric Stafford’s automobile addiction began before he could walk, and it has fueled his passion to write news, reviews, and more for Car and Driver since 2016. His aspiration growing up was to become a millionaire with a Jay Leno–like car collection. Apparently, getting rich is harder than social-media influencers make it seem, so he avoided financial success entirely to become an automotive journalist and drive new cars for a living. After earning a journalism degree at Central Michigan University and working at a daily newspaper, the years of basically burning money on failed project cars and lemon-flavored jalopies finally paid off when Car and Driver hired him. His garage currently includes a 2010 Acura RDX, a manual '97 Chevy Camaro Z/28, and a '90 Honda CRX Si.

title: Audi Axes The Luxurious A8 After 32 Years
raw_summary: Plummeting sales and an aging platform spelled the end of the road for Audi's flagship sedan After 32 years and four generations, the Audi A8 has ended production. article_paragraphs: Plummeting sales and an aging platform spelled the end of the road for Audi's flagship sedan

After 32 years and four generations, the Audi A8 has ended production. The final example of this flagship luxury sedan rolled off the Neckarsulm factory in Germany in mid-October, after Audi stopped taking orders for the car earlier in the year. With the A8 dead, the Mercedes-Benz S-Class and BMW 7 Series now have one less rival to worry about.

The original A8 debuted in early 1994, and two years later, Audi released the more powerful S8 version, equipping it with an upgraded naturally aspirated 4.2-liter V8 delivering 355 horsepower. The A8 was also famously sold with a 6.0-liter W12. In late 2002, the second-generation A8 launched and was sold with several different engines, including a V6 petrol, V8 petrol, V10, W12, and even two V6 and V8 diesels.

Through its third and fourth generations, the Audi A8 remained a popular option for those in the market for a high-end, luxury sedan. However, in more recent years, it has started to feel a little dated compared to the newer Mercedes-Benz S-Class and BMW 7 Series. The current-gen S-Class was launched in 2020 and was recently updated for the 2027 model year , while the current 7 Series hit the market in 2022. By comparison, the fourth-gen A8 dates back to 2017.

The end of A8 production leaves a hole in Audi's line-up. Somewhat filling the void left by the A8 will be the new Audi Q9 , the company's long-awaited rival to the Mercedes-Benz GLS and BMW X7. It's significantly bigger than the Q7 and is shaping up to be the company's most luxurious new model. Audi will sell the Q9 in six- and seven-seat configurations and has fitted it with a huge panoramic glass roof with advanced ambient lighting, a whole host of plush materials, up to three screens on the dashboard, and MagSafe wireless chargers.

Though no direct successor to the A8 has been confirmed, Audi may have something up its sleeve. Auto Motor und Sport believes the German brand is in talks with Huawei to use its vehicle architecture for a new luxury sedan in China. Details about this new model are limited, including whether or not it will be sold outside of China. If this model does see the light of day, it would follow in the footsteps of other Chinese-built Audi models, most notably the E5 Sportback and E7X sold under the capitalized AUDI brand and co-developed with SAIC Motor.

Sales of the plush Audi A8 began to dry up toward the end of its lifecycle. Sales of the luxury sedan peaked at over 6,000 units in the U.S. in 2013, but they have been steadily declining ever since. In 2025, just 1,406 were sold. By comparison, BMW sold 11,393 examples of the 7 Series in the U.S. in 2025, while Mercedes sold 7,408 S-Class models.

raw_title: The New Lotus Esprit Supercar Will Be Powered by a 670-HP V-8
title: The New Lotus Esprit Supercar Will Be Powered by a 670-HP V-8
raw_summary: There’s a new V-8-powered Lotus on the way, and we’ve just got our first proper look at the powertrain. While the supercar uses the codename Type 135, most of the world expects it to resurrect the British brand’s legendary Espirt nameplate, and now we know that it’ll have a brand-new 4.0-liter V-8. The engine will team up with a dual-clutch automatic transmission, and both will be built by a company called Horse Powertrain. The twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8, called the Horse W40, will come in a hot-V configuration, meaning it’ll store its turbos between the cylinder banks, rather than on either side of them. Horse says the combustion half of the powertrain will be responsible for generating 670 horsepower and 590 pound-feet of torque, though it’ll be part of a larger hybrid system that Lotus promises will combine for at least 986 horsepower. With the engine weighing just 441 pounds, that’s quite a power-dense mill.

Horse also says the engine was designed from the ground up with the hybrid configuration in mind, which required special consideration. Rather than pair it with another company’s transmission, Horse built its own eight-speed dual-clutch automatic called the Horse 8LDCT. The gearbox features a sports car-grade wet dual clutch, which is claimed to enable sub-20-millisecond shift responses, along with a silicon-carbide control system and a variable-displacement mechanical pump.

Horse’s new powertrain components will make their debut on what’s expected to be the upcoming Lotus Esprit. Unfortunately, the car’s production is still some time away, with Lotus planning to reveal and launch the model in 2028.

raw_title: Lucid CEO admits it ‘did not even know where cars were’ and lost orders
title: Lucid CEO admits it 'did not even know where cars were' and lost orders
raw_summary: Lucid (LCID) CEO Silvio Napoli admitted on the company’s Q3 earnings call that, as recently as this summer, the automaker “did not even know where cars were.” Buyers placed orders, Lucid took up to two weeks to locate and deliver a car, and some of those buyers walked away. That’s a rough admission from a company sitting on thousands of unsold vehicles. And it’s a problem Tesla ran into, and fixed, back in 2018 at more than ten times Lucid’s current volume.
summary: Lucid (LCID) CEO Silvio Napoli admitted on the company’s Q3 earnings call that, as recently as this summer, the automaker “did not even know where cars were.” Buyers placed orders, Lucid took up to two weeks to locate and deliver a car, and some of those buyers walked away.
article_paragraphs: Lucid (LCID) CEO Silvio Napoli admitted on the company’s Q3 earnings call that, as recently as this summer, the automaker “did not even know where cars were.” Buyers placed orders, Lucid took up to two weeks to locate and deliver a car, and some of those buyers walked away.
That’s a rough admission from a company sitting on thousands of unsold vehicles. And it’s a problem Tesla ran into, and fixed, back in 2018 at more than ten times Lucid’s current volume.

Napoli made the comment when an analyst asked whether Lucid’s deliveries would go up or down in the fourth quarter. He said that at the start of Q3, the company had orders where it “would take sometimes two weeks to deliver to the customer, and so we would lose the order.”

He said Lucid now has visibility on which cars are being built, where they’re shipped, where they’re stored, and when they can reach a customer. A new commercial team also now sells the cars it knows are available on the day a customer wants one.

Lucid built 3,228 more vehicles than it delivered in the first half of 2026, including 5,500 built but only 3,093 delivered in Q1. Its inventory hit $1.38 billion on the balance sheet at the end of June, which is why we reported earlier this year that Lucid had to adjust production after a bloated Q1 inventory .
So Lucid had thousands of cars on lots and in transit, and it was still losing buyers because it couldn’t match a car to an order fast enough.

In Q3, Lucid cut production to 2,954 vehicles and delivered 3,806 , down 7% year over year. Finished goods inventory fell by almost 15% during the quarter, according to new CFO Alexander De Bock. Inventory stood at $1.22 billion on September 30.
Tesla learned this lesson the hard way during the Model 3 ramp.

title: These Two Porsche 911s Are Both Hiding Powerful V8s
raw_summary: A V8-powered Porsche 911 may sound like a bad idea. However, last month, an Australian firm crafted a wild, twin-turbocharged V8 example and set it up for drifting. Not to be outdone, a pair of modified Porsche 911s with V8 engines have been unveiled at SEMA by Eneos, and they're just as excessive. The first is a 2007 Porsche 911 GT3 built by Faruk Kugay from Devspeed. Kugay purchased this GT3 several years ago and, in 2023, fitted it with a bespoke widebody kit and Subaru's famous turbocharged 2.5-liter EJ25 boxer four-cylinder. Now, it's undergone a second engine swap and has been morphed into a wild drift machine.
summary: A V8-powered Porsche 911 may sound like a bad idea. However, last month, an Australian firm crafted a wild, twin-turbocharged V8 example and set it up for drifting. Not to be outdone, a pair of modified Porsche 911s with V8 engines have been unveiled at SEMA by Eneos, and they're just as excessive.
article_paragraphs: A V8-powered Porsche 911 may sound like a bad idea. However, last month, an Australian firm crafted a wild, twin-turbocharged V8 example and set it up for drifting. Not to be outdone, a pair of modified Porsche 911s with V8 engines have been unveiled at SEMA by Eneos, and they're just as excessive.

The first is a 2007 Porsche 911 GT3 built by Faruk Kugay from Devspeed. Kugay purchased this GT3 several years ago and, in 2023, fitted it with a bespoke widebody kit and Subaru's famous turbocharged 2.5-liter EJ25 boxer four-cylinder. Now, it's undergone a second engine swap and has been morphed into a wild drift machine.

The Subaru engine has been replaced with a naturally aspirated 6.0-liter LS2 V8 that has somehow been crammed into the 911's small engine bay. The centerpiece of the new powertrain is a custom exhaust with CNC-bent header tubes crafted by German engineer Christian Koegler. The exhaust pokes out from above the engine bay where the 911's rear window would normally be. It looks like a work of art, and is functional too.

Mated to the V8 is a manual transmission from a Porsche 996 Turbo, a two-way limited-slip differential, custom suspension components, a Link ECU, and a widebody kit. As the car has been built to go drifting, the interior has been stripped out and includes a roll cage and a pair of lightweight carbon fiber racing seats.

The second Porsche 911 on display at the Eneos SEMA booth is a 1978 Porsche 911 SC from Jimmy Oakes. It's powered by a Ferrari F136 V8 used in models like the Maserati Quattroporte and has custom independent throttle bodies based on parts from the E92 BMW M3's V8. Like the GT3, the 911 SC has a manual transmission from a 996-generation 911 and upgraded Porsche Boxster brakes.

A special widebody kit has been developed for the car that dramatically enhances its stance on the road. A fresh coat of Guards Red paint adds to the dramatic look, as does the lack of a front bumper. Sitting in place of the rear bumper is a custom-made stainless steel exhaust. A set of 17-inch Volk Racing wheels completes the car's wild transformation.

According to Oakes, his 911 SC's design draws on Japan's tuning and motorsport culture. If he wants to double down on the JDM style, perhaps in the future he could swap that Italian V8 for the Nissan Skyline GT-R's iconic RB26 inline-six?

Across all new vehicles, the average hit a record $51,109, up 1.3% from September and 2.1% year over year, even as prices rose more slowly than they typically do in October.

EV incentives barely budged from September’s revised 11.2% of the average transaction price to 11.3% in October. That’s up from 10.3% a year earlier and well above October’s industrywide average of 6.8%.

Tesla’s average selling price fell from September to $54,194, but it was still up 1.2% year over year. The Cybertruck helped push that average higher. Cox Automotive estimates Tesla sold 1,914 Cybertrucks in October, its best month in more than a year, at an average price of $92,380.
About 40 trucks per state? That is way too many. I am not sure if my eyes can handle it.
The strange thing is that I see more Cybertruck around me being driven by Tesla Energy than regular Cybertruck owners.

That sales bump comes as Tesla prepares to end Cybertruck production at its Austin factory in mid-2027. Elon Musk said Tesla will dismantle the assembly line around June or July to make room for more Cybercab robotaxis.

After unveiling the Yangwang Altior in the UAE on Monday, its new ultra-luxury flagship electric sedan, BYD showcased its latest breakthrough technology.
The Chinese automaker launched a new integrated charging system in the Abu Dhabi desert that brings BYD’s “Three Green Dreams” to life.

In 2006, BYD president and CEO Wang Chuanfu revealed his vision of “Three Green Dreams,” including harnessing solar power to generate renewable energy, storing that energy in batteries, and replacing gas-powered vehicles with electric ones that run on clean energy.
The new charging system is the “world’s first,” according to BYD, to integrate solar power generation, energy storage, Flash Charging, and robotic charging together in one solution.

BYD’s Flash Charging tech enables a vehicle’s battery to charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes, essentially the same time it takes to fill up at a gas station. For a full recharge, or to go from 10% to 97%, it takes just nine minutes.
The new robotic charging arm automatically locates the vehicle’s charging port, opens its cover, plugs in, and then removes it once the session is over.
By combining robotic charging with its Automated Valet Parking, BYD said the new tech goes beyond automated driving and parking to the charging process itself.

raw_title: Norway’s Electric Snowplow Worked. Sweden Added Hydrogen Anyway.
title: Norway's Electric Snowplow Worked. Sweden Added Hydrogen Anyway
raw_summary: Norway has already demonstrated battery-electric snowplowing on one of its toughest mountain highways. A Scania 45 R covered roughly 7,000 km on Hardangervidda, plowing, grading and spreading sand through a Norwegian winter. Its performance exceeded expectations. Meanwhile, Sweden has unveiled a hydrogen snowplow that is, in fact, another large battery-electric truck, with a fuel cell and hydrogen tanks added for extra range. The engineering question is why that second energy system is worth having when batteries are already doing the work, and when a conventional generator running on renewable diesel could offer a simpler, potentially cheaper route to occasional extended operation. The Swedish vehicle has to compete with more than diesel snowplows. My full TFIE Strategy Briefing examines Norway’s measured electric operation, China’s expanding snow-removal equipment market and the additional costs hydrogen must justify.
summary: Norway has already demonstrated battery-electric snowplowing on one of its toughest mountain highways. A Scania 45 R covered roughly 7,000 km on Hardangervidda, plowing, grading and spreading sand through a Norwegian winter. Meanwhile, Sweden has unveiled a hydrogen snowplow that is, in fact, another large battery-electric truck, with a fuel cell and hydrogen tanks added for extra range.
article_paragraphs: Norway has already demonstrated battery-electric snowplowing on one of its toughest mountain highways. A Scania 45 R covered roughly 7,000 km on Hardangervidda, plowing, grading and spreading sand through a Norwegian winter. Its performance exceeded expectations. Meanwhile, Sweden has unveiled a hydrogen snowplow that is, in fact, another large battery-electric truck, with a fuel cell and hydrogen tanks added for extra range. The engineering question is why that second energy system is worth having when batteries are already doing the work, and when a conventional generator running on renewable diesel could offer a simpler, potentially cheaper route to occasional extended operation.

The Swedish vehicle has to compete with more than diesel snowplows. My full TFIE Strategy Briefing examines Norway’s measured electric operation, China’s expanding snow-removal equipment market and the additional costs hydrogen must justify.

Sweden’s project brings together Scania, MaserFrakt and Peab. The vehicle carries a 356 kWh rechargeable battery and 56 kg of hydrogen. The fuel cell generates electricity to extend the truck’s operating time between charging sessions. That gives the vehicle two energy-storage systems, plus the equipment to convert hydrogen into electricity. It will still need electric charging, and it will also need hydrogen production, delivery, storage and refueling.

Norway’s experience makes the starting point uncomfortable for hydrogen advocates. The Norwegian Public Roads Administration’s 2025 trial demonstrated that a production-based heavy electric truck could do demanding winter-maintenance work. Its measured consumption averaged approximately 2.02 kWh/km, with around six and a half hours of operating endurance under evaluated mixed-duty conditions. The trial identified shortcomings in charging compatibility and payload, but these were engineering and operating problems to resolve, not evidence that battery-electric snowplows were incapable of doing the job.

China is moving toward broader deployment. Municipalities have used smaller electric snow-removal equipment for years, while manufacturers have developed full-sized specialized electric vehicles. Beijing’s Mentougou district awarded contracts for 24 multifunction snow-removal trucks in September 2026. The final chassis specifications have not all been confirmed as battery-electric, but the procurement demonstrates a market moving beyond isolated demonstrations.

China’s much larger battery-electric truck industry is also providing specialized equipment manufacturers with an expanding supply of powertrains, batteries and heavy-duty chassis. Electric snowplows benefit from components developed and manufactured for freight vehicles at much greater volumes.

The Swedish approach looks increasingly difficult to justify against that background. If six or seven hours of productive operation is adequate, a battery-electric truck can already do the work. If longer shifts are required, larger batteries, better charging arrangements, mobile charging equipment or operational changes deserve assessment first. Hydrogen cannot claim the extreme-duty market merely because charging requires planning.

There is another alternative that the hydrogen comparison tends to omit. A conventional generator running on hydrotreated vegetable oil, or HVO, could supply additional electricity when the battery needs support. Diesel generators, fuel tanks and liquid-fuel distribution systems are mature technologies. Major generator manufacturers already approve suitable equipment for HVO, which can use conventional diesel-type storage and handling systems. Integrating a generator into a particular electric truck still requires engineering, certification and emissions controls, but it avoids constructing a hydrogen supply chain for a small fleet of seasonal vehicles.

A bespoke, naturally aspirated, 8.3-liter V-16 engine nestled into its carbon-fiber body structure behind the driver cements that fact, churning out 986 horsepower on its own. Inside, the Tourbillon eschews large infotainment screens and extensive driver aids for expertly milled switchgear, top-shelf materials, and a more connected driving experience—a choice that its Audemars-Piguet-wearing clientele will surely appreciate.

VinFast is probably a brand name you’ve not heard before, and that’s because the Vietnam-based company has been selling electric SUVs here for only a few years. The VF8, introduced in 2023, hasn’t sold in significant numbers. In fact, there were no 2026 VF8s, but after skipping a model year, it's back for 2027.

The VF8 is compelling on paper, with a long list of standard amenities and an attractive starting price. All models are all-wheel drive and feature two electric motors generating 349 or 402 horsepower, depending on trim. It's on the road where things quickly fall apart. The VF8’s road manners are rough, its driving range is uncompetitive with similarly priced rival EV SUVs, and its onboard infotainment tech is a nightmare of unintuitive menus and software bugs.
Expert Tip: If an affordable, scienced-out electric SUV with decent range and a long warranty is what you’re after, consider the Hyundai Ioniq 5 or the Kia EV6 instead.

After taking the 2026 model year off, the VF8 is back, sporting a lower starting price. The Eco trim’s $41,790 ask represents a $5410 drop from the 2025 model, and the Plus’s $46,990 price is $6010 less than it was previously. VinFast has improved the VF8’s driver-assistance offerings this year too, adding rear automated emergency braking, an intersection assist system, an automatic lane-changing feature, evasive steering assist, and a feature that will bring the car to a stop if it detects that the driver has become unresponsive.

If this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

An all-wheel-drive electric powertrain with two electric motors makes 349 horsepower in the Eco trim and 402 horsepower in the Plus model. While acceleration is respectable for a compact electric SUV, the VF8 falls short in other, subjective areas. For example, the VF8 we sampled was bouncy on uneven roads and its steering required too much effort.
In Comparison: The VF8 Plus’s 60 mph time in our testing is a half second behind the less powerful, 320-hp Hyundai Ioniq 5 .

Sure, it's not a straight rip-off, but place your fingers over the lights and grille, and you have to admit there's an uncomfortable similarity between the designs.

News of the raid broke at the weekend, only days before BYD and Jaguar Land Rover head to court in The Hague. But The Times reports that it happened back in August, when JLR's legal team hoped it would find documentary evidence of BYD reverse engineering a Defender before any files were destroyed.

JLR has every right to be concerned. It's not just that the Ti7 looks very similar to the Defender, but that BYD's version costs thousands less. The Chinese SUV starts at £47,995 ($64,300) in the UK, but a base Defender 110 will set you back over £16,000 ($21,500 more). European Ti7s come with a BYD "Super Hybrid" powertrain that combines a 1.5-liter inline-4 and four electric motors to generate 402 hp (408 PS). Zero to 62 mph (100 kmh) takes 4.8 seconds, and the 35.6 kWh battery is claimed to deliver 74 miles (119 km) of range. As a package, it's a real threat to JLR.

The Defender isn't the only JLR SUV with a doppelgänger. The 7 SUV built by Chery's Jaecoo brand has been dubbed the "Temu Range Rover" for its low price and visual similarity to the Range Rover Freelander and Evoque. The recipe has been a big hit with European buyers, who snapped up so many SUVs that the Jaecoo 7 became the first Chinese vehicle ever to top the UK car sales chart. But so far JLR hasn't instigated legal action.

It did, however, take China's Jiangling Motor Corporation (JMC) to court in 2016 over the similarity between that automaker's $19,000 Landwind X7 and JLR's own $54,000 first-generation Evoque. The court ruled JMC had copied five distinct Evoque design details and found in JLR's favor, forcing an immediate halt of X7 production. JLR argued that the X7 was confusing customers. Though maybe they were just confused about why JLR was asking them to pay more than double for the real thing.

The Landwind X7 was one of dozens of Western designs copied by Chinese brands who were struggling to find their own identity in the early years of the new millennium. Others included the Zotye SR8, a homage to the Porsche Macan. But it's not only the vehicle designs themselves that get the Xerox treatment. Earlier this year, Great Wall Motor's (GWM) chairman Wei Jiangjun publicly apologized after his company published an advert for its Wey V9X SUV that was a blatant copy of an ad JLR produced to promote the Range Rover Sport.

"There can be no justification," Jiangjun said, and he vowed to take "full legal and financial responsibility" for the gaffe. It doesn't look like BYD is ready to do the same, but the court in the Netherlands might force its hand.

Jaguar Land Rover thinks BYD is pinching its designs too.

raw_summary: The first thing that comes to mind when you mention Quattro is probably Audi's 1980 Group B rally car. The 1982 World Rally Championship runner-up still looked at home behind the wheel of the 493-horsepower rally monster.

Audi's new ad campaign titled "Performance Runs in the Family" features a pair of videos: a typical 30-second TV spot, and a 4-minute short with Mouton driving a Quattro S1 up Pikes Peak. During the visually stunning drive up the Colorado mountain, she reminisced about the animosity she faced during the 1985 hill climb, her winning run, and how the ascent has changed in the 41 years since.

Mouton was the first woman and the first non-American to win the Pikes Peak International Hill Climb . The Frenchwoman set a record time of 11:25.390 up the treacherous 12.4-mile ascent, besting the previous record set by Al Unser Jr. in 1983 by 13 seconds. Mouton is still effortlessly cool, still delivering pointed one-liners as naturally as the rest of us breathe. During the revival run, she noted, "When I was at this spot in the race, I had no time for feelings."

The 30-second TV spot mixes archival footage of Mouton during the Group B era with footage of a 2027 Audi SQ7 driving up Pikes Peak. To emphasize the campaign's legacy theme, the ad features Mouton alongside her daughter, Jessica. The third-generation Q7 isn't as nimble on the twisting mountain roads as a Group B rally car, but that isn't the point. The SUV's new styling looks just as aggressive and far more comfortable for a family. Vito Paladino, Audi of America's President, stated in a release:

"Audi's story of quattro didn't end with rally racing. That connection between performance and everyday capability is what makes quattro such a defining part of our brand. The all-new Audi Q7 family carries that legacy forward, bringing together Audi's performance heritage with the innovation and engineering that define the next generation of our vehicles."

The 1985 Pikes Peak International Hill Climb was Mouton's last event with Audi before she departed for her farewell season with Peugeot. The Frenchwoman and her accomplishments will forever be tied to Audi. Mouton's four WRC victories with the Audi Quattro are a legacy every four-wheel-drive model produced by the German automaker inherits. It's not merely laurels to rest on, but a level of performance that Audi has to honor.

title: GM Wants Its AI To Drag Race For You
raw_summary: It seems General Motors wants to give owners of its vehicles every possible advantage at the drag strip. Rather than leaving it up to owners to perfectly time a drag strip's Christmas tree, a new GM patent describes a system that can automatically launch a car off the line as soon as the lights turn green. If the system works as described, Chevy owners may never again have to explain to their Ford rivals that a slow launch was the reason they lost a race. GM filed a patent for its launch control assistant in January 2025 and was granted the patent earlier this month. The system uses front-facing cameras to detect the iconic Christmas tree lights at a drag strip. When the cameras notice these iconic red, orange, and green lights, it'll tell the driver to activate launch control.
summary: It seems General Motors wants to give owners of its vehicles every possible advantage at the drag strip. Rather than leaving it up to owners to perfectly time a drag strip's Christmas tree, a new GM patent describes a system that can automatically launch a car off the line as soon as the lights turn green.
article_paragraphs: It seems General Motors wants to give owners of its vehicles every possible advantage at the drag strip. Rather than leaving it up to owners to perfectly time a drag strip's Christmas tree, a new GM patent describes a system that can automatically launch a car off the line as soon as the lights turn green. If the system works as described, Chevy owners may never again have to explain to their Ford rivals that a slow launch was the reason they lost a race.

GM filed a patent for its launch control assistant in January 2025 and was granted the patent earlier this month. The system uses front-facing cameras to detect the iconic Christmas tree lights at a drag strip. When the cameras notice these iconic red, orange, and green lights, it'll tell the driver to activate launch control.

Like in pretty much any car, the driver will do this by stomping on the brake pedal and then flooring the accelerator. The car's onboard systems then take over. Rather than requiring the driver to keep both pedals floored and then lift off the brake the moment the light turns green, GM's system does all the work for them and builds torque in the engine while keeping the brakes slammed in position.

Trick onboard software will quickly determine the sequence of the yellow lights and release brake pressure the moment the green light appears. In addition, the patent has the ability to automatically detect different drag light designs that illuminate the lights at unique intervals, ensuring the driver gets the best possible launch regardless of the drag strip and the location. It's unclear when the driver will have to get back on the throttle or if the car can keep the accelerator pinned all the way down the quarter-mile.

Car manufacturers routinely patent intriguing systems and technologies . Some of them hit the market, while others are too far-fetched and never see the light of day. GM's latest patent sounds quite achievable, and we're sure it'd be well-received by many performance car enthusiasts. On the flip side, drag racing traditionalists may not feel particularly keen about handing over the control of their car to its onboard systems.

It also wouldn't be very fair to race a car with a system like this against one where the driver is in full control . It takes a lot of experience to minimize reaction times at the drag strip and pull away at the exact right moment. One of the key tricks to get the perfect launch isn't to wait for the green light to appear before getting off the line. Instead, experienced drag racers anticipate the amber lights and often launch when the final amber light appears. By the time their eyes notice the amber light and their feet lift off the brakes and hit the throttle, the green light has flashed up. One could argue modern launch control systems are already a form of cheating, and GM's even more advanced system takes this to a new level.

article_paragraphs: The Cobra badge is back for what might be a GT350 replacement

When is a Mustang GT350 not a Mustang GT350? When it's a Mustang Cobra. Yesterday we reported on rumors that Ford was readying a high-winding successor to the 2015-20 GT350 , and now we know that car will resurrect the Cobra badge. We even know exactly how it will sound, and well: dribble.

A teaser video published to Ford Racing's Instagram account features text slowly spelling out the word "Cobra" while an evil-sounding V8 sings in the background. Small pause as each shift bangs home telling us the motor is backed by a manual transmission. Oh my. Where do we sign?
"You'll want to hear this," says the text accompanying the video. "For the drivers, with an all-motor heart born from racing. Ford Mustang Cobra, a Legacy Reborn. The story continues in 2027."
So Cobra it is, which makes sense, because Ford's licensing deal with Shelby died a few years back, and Shelby now sells its own tuned Mustang with GT350 badges.

And we might even be in line for not one, but two Cobras. The letter R in "Cobra" is highlighted in two separate points in the video, the final time in Ford Racing's trademark blue color. That suggests Ford is preparing Cobra and Cobra R versions of the Mustang, just like it did in the 1990s and early 2000s.

Cobra name aside, Ford's social post mostly tallies with the story we wrote earlier this week about Ford building a successor to the S550-generation GT350 and GT350 R. Those cars featured a naturally aspirated 5.2-liter Voodoo engine with a flat-plane crank V8 design most commonly used by supercar brands like Ferrari and McLaren. They made 526 hp and redlined at 8,250 rpm, but were phased out after 2020.

We can't know for sure if the engine fitted to the Cobra also has a flat-plane crank, but it sure sounds like it could. And it doesn't sound turbocharged or supercharged. The engine bark is too crisp for our ears. Most blown V8s sound slightly muffled, and the frequencies are bass-heavy, but this has real bite with no supercharger whine. Some rumors suggest Ford is going to homologate the 5.4-liter V8 from its Mustang GT3 race cars for road duties. That engine is limited to a maximum of 550 hp under FIA Balance of Performance rules, which isn't much more than the 500 hp the naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 in the Dark Horse makes. But those rules wouldn't apply to street cars.

article_paragraphs: The new factory will anchor Honda’s hybrid push, and it could build some big new SUVs.

Honda is betting big on hybrids in North America and has announced it will build a $3 billion factory in Ohio focusing on new hybrid models. The new site will join its existing operations in Ohio, which include the Anna Engine Plant and the Honda Transmission Plant-Ohio. It will also increase the brand's U.S. manufacturing capacity to roughly 1.3 million vehicles a year.

The new factory will be positioned near Honda's other Ohio auto plants and is expected to begin production in 2029. It will employ more than 2,000 workers and be capable of building up to 240,000 vehicles a year. The site is set to play a crucial role in Honda and Acura's plans to launch 15 new hybrid models globally by the end of the decade, with a particular focus on the North American market.

Honda says the factory will incorporate "leading-edge automation, data-driven technologies and flexible production systems" to be one of the most advanced factories of its kind in the world. Traditional gasoline-powered models will be built alongside new hybrids at the site, and the plant will also be flexible enough to produce battery-electric vehicles.

In addition to locking in an all-new factory for Ohio, Honda is retooling the Anna Engine Plant to build a new four-cylinder engine destined for compact and midsize vehicles built in North America. The Honda Transmission Plant-Ohio is also being updated to support two next-generation Honda hybrid powertrains. These hybrids will first be used by compact and midsize vehicles starting next year, before production of a hybrid setup for larger models starts "in the coming years." Honda has also confirmed it is retooling the Alabama Auto Plant site to boost vehicle production and manufacture a new hybrid V6.

The Japanese company hasn't specified which of its vehicles will be built at the new Ohio plant. A September report on Honda's planned Ohio hybrid factory indicated that the next-generation Acura MDX could be built at the plant, as could Acura's upcoming three-row, eight-seat SUV. The same report suggested that Honda itself may also build the rumored "Pilot XXL" at the same Ohio factory.

Honda's next-generation hybrid system was previewed late last year and includes a new lightweight platform. The fifth-generation hybrid system is expected to debut with the new CR-V and should include a 2.0-liter four-cylinder working alongside a pair of updated electric motors. All models using Honda's new hybrid powertrain should also get the same S+ Shift system as the new Prelude, which simulates traditional gear shifts. Honda is targeting more than 10% better fuel economy and a 30% reduction in production costs compared with the current powertrain.

Similar advancements are expected with Honda's new V6 hybrid. It was also showcased last November and pairs the new V6 with up to three electric motors in all-wheel-drive models. Honda says models with this powertrain should accelerate 10% quicker than current non-hybrid V6 models and deliver a 30% improvement in fuel economy.

BMW's venerable 3-series sports sedan is now complemented by an electric variant called the i3 , which rides on the same new 800-volt architecture as the iX3 SUV. The i3 will also spawn the first proper electric M car, with the electric M3 expected to pack a potent quad-motor powertrain. The i3 goes on sale in the U.S. at the end of 2026, and we expect the electric M3 to follow in 2027.

Pickup trucks are big business in the United States, and Chevy is overhauling its moneymaker for 2027. The next-generation Silverado goes on sale by the end of 2026 with reworked styling that doesn't stray far from the current generation's assertive look. The big changes are under the skin, where the turbocharged four-cylinder and Duramax diesel are joined by two new small-block V-8s, one measuring 5.7 liters and the other at 6.6 liters. We're still waiting on power figures for the new V-8s, but they are expected to be more efficient than the engines they replace. The cabin also gets far more modern with a new 16.3-inch touchscreen and a 12.2-inch digital gauge cluster that are standard across the lineup.

The Chevy Camaro is set to make a triumphant return for the 2029 model year. The iconic pony car will likely return with two doors, but there's a strong chance that Chevy offers it in a four-door configuration too, since it will share a platform with new sedans from Buick and Cadillac. A turbocharged four-cylinder engine will likely be the base powertrain, while the Camaro is also expected to borrow the new 535-hp 6.7-liter V-8 from the Corvette. A 10-speed automatic will hopefully be joined by a six-speed manual. Production is expected to kick off in late 2028, and the starting price will probably be around $40,000.

Just as the Hemi V-8 returned to the Ram 1500 pickup truck, so too will the eight-cylinder squeeze its way back under the hood of the Dodge Charger . The electric Charger Daytona has failed to catch on, and the return of the V-8 should help the muscle car regain the adoration of the Dodge fanbase. The V-8 will likely be reintroduced in 5.7-liter, 6.4-liter, and Hellcat-badged supercharged 6.2-liter form, and power outputs should remain mostly the same, with the Hellcat easily topping 700 ponies. Look for the Hemi V-8 to reappear in the Charger sometime in 2027.

title: The new BMW i3 just proved how efficient an EV can be after a nearly 3,700-mile road trip
raw_summary: Who says long EV road trips mean hours at charging stations? BMW drove the new i3 for over 3 days, covering nearly 3,700 miles, and it took less than 3 hours of charging. BMW put the i3 to the ultimate test of efficiency, charging speed, and long-distance EV capability on a nearly 3,700-mile Pan-European journey.

article_paragraphs: Who says long EV road trips mean hours at charging stations? BMW drove the new i3 for over 3 days, covering nearly 3,700 miles, and it took less than 3 hours of charging.
BMW put the i3 to the ultimate test of efficiency, charging speed, and long-distance EV capability on a nearly 3,700-mile Pan-European journey.

The Paneurpeana, as it’s called, is considered the benchmark for range and charging speed. The route begins at the North Cape in Norway, the northernmost point of continental Europe you can reach by car, and ends in Tarifa, Spain, the southernmost point of mainland Europe.
BMW drove the new i3 50 xDrive for a total of 3,658 miles (5,886.7 km) across eight countries and spent just 2 hours, 45 minutes, and 54 seconds charging at an average of 275 kW.
The performance beat the previous record by more than seven hours, according to Mike Reichelt, head of BMW’s Neue Klasse
BMW said the charging points were not predetermined and that it had to account for external factors such as weather and traffic jams.
The new i3 was impressively efficient during the trip, consuming an average of just 12.5 kWh per 100 km, beating its official WLTP combined energy consumption of 18-13.4 kWh/100 km.
BMW said the trip took 3 days, 2 hours, and 41 minutes, with an average speed of 79.7 km/h, and that the i3 was charged exclusively at public charging points across national charging networks.

summary: Garmin and Waze are teaming up on an interesting new safety feature that could give cyclists a little extra protection when sharing the road with cars – by making cyclists themselves show up in Waze. The new feature allows cyclists using a compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin smartwatch to share their location through Garmin’s LiveTrack feature.
article_paragraphs: Garmin and Waze are teaming up on an interesting new safety feature that could give cyclists a little extra protection when sharing the road with cars – by making cyclists themselves show up in Waze.

The new feature allows cyclists using a compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin smartwatch to share their location through Garmin’s LiveTrack feature. That location can then appear in real time to nearby drivers using Waze, with cyclists displayed as moving icons on the road.

As someone who recently joined the Garmin family myself with a smartwatch for tracking my cycling, running, and other activities, this is exactly the type of feature I love seeing added to the platform.
I’ve long maintained that safety – or more accurately, the perception that cycling isn’t safe – is one of the biggest impediments to getting more people onto bikes.

That’s especially true in the US, where cyclists are often forced to share roads with cars instead of enjoying the kind of widespread separated cycling infrastructure found in many more bike-friendly countries. And when a cyclist and a multi-ton vehicle have to occupy the same space, making sure the driver knows that cyclist is there can make a big difference.
Of course, an icon on Waze isn’t going to magically make cycling safe. It won’t replace protected bike lanes, better road design, slower vehicle speeds, or attentive drivers.

But I can certainly imagine situations where it could help. Riding at night or in poor visibility, approaching a blind curve, or simply traveling on a narrow road where a driver might otherwise come upon a cyclist unexpectedly are all situations where an advance warning could be useful.

The feature is opt-in through Garmin Connect and activates when the cyclist starts an outdoor cycling activity. Garmin says location sharing is temporary and session-based, and that cyclists’ personal information isn’t displayed in Waze. Of course, anyone who uses a personal GPS device has already accepted that their location is shared with Big Tech in exchange for features they value, but at least we know that any personalized info stays within Garmin instead of proliferating even further.

title: Rewarding for the Right Owner: 1979 Lancia Zagato Tested
raw_summary: He’d been studying the little Lancia through the window as we rummaged through his parts store in search of a you-wire-it cigarette lighter we could graft into the car’s electrical system. The on-board lighter socket had proved incompatible with our Escort’s plug. He considered that piece of informa­tion as we paid for the lighter, then tried to sell us a can of engine additive as we made for the door. The dogeared display for the pour-in miracle claimed it would do everything short of putting you in the winner’s circle at Daytona. article_paragraphs: He’d been studying the little Lancia through the window as we rummaged through his parts store in search of a you-wire-it cigarette lighter we could graft into the car’s electrical system. The on-board lighter socket had proved incompatible with our Escort’s plug.

He considered that piece of informa­tion as we paid for the lighter, then tried to sell us a can of engine additive as we made for the door. The dogeared display for the pour-in miracle claimed it would do everything short of putting you in the winner’s circle at Daytona. In the old days, in different packaging, it probably sold as a cure for rheumatism, lice, warts, heaves, halitosis, and hard hearing. He patted the uppermost can and his voice trailed us into the drizzly afternoon, hinting of impending doom.

He had a point there, but we forsook the additive and let the door close be­hind us. We hooked up the Escort and set out into the growing evening rain­storm in search of a major mechanical or electrical failure to get pissed off about. The further we got from Dayto­na, spearing out into the chilly, desert­ed, water-swept two-lanes of central Florida, howling into the gloom at a steady 80, the clearer our second thoughts became. What if Lancia’s self­-incriminating talk of a “new high-quali­ty modular electrical system through­out” was just a hoax? We didn’t even have an umbrella. Would the modular electrics leave us sinking in the middle of some non-modular backwater swamp? Would the shift linkage come adrift? Would the carburetion cease to carburet, or the ignition cease to ignite? These were fits of pique visited upon us by Lancias before. But the Zagato did none of the above. Oh, the letdown, not to be able to tell you we had to hitch­hike out of the Glades in the back of a sagging half-ton Ford pickup.

Times have apparently changed at Lancia. While we can’t say the thrashing we dealt our Zagato was the equivalent of 50,000 miles’ worth of normal driv­ing, the car suffered us, if not gladly, at least with no crippling catastrophes. Its shortcomings fell more in the area of nuisance value, an area offset by the fun of driving the car under the right cir­cumstances. As often happens with cars of strong character, the Zagato’s car-to-­owner-to-car relationship becomes a high-spirited adversary relationship, an exchange of sometimes conflicting, sometime parallel philosophies. This re­lationship can make a Lancia Zagato a rewarding car for the right owner. All that remains is to determine whether ownership then qualifies him as a 24-ka­rat eccentric in good standing, or simply a lover of good fun.

Fun is what Lancia had in mind when it contracted Carrozzeria Zagato to cre­ate and build a coachbuilt steel targa body for the existing Beta Coupe. The unit-bodied result is an interesting com­bination of a normal lift-off fiberglass targa roof panel and an everyday roadster’s fold-down vinyl rear roof and plastic window. The targa bar that re­mains after everything else is lifted off or folded down provides sturdy rollover protection, enhanced by horizontal out­er roofline struts that connect the bar with the windshield pillars. Four configurations are possible by adding or re­moving the roof components and roll­ing windows up or down.

The resulting greenhouse possesses all the elegance of a railroad shanty and thwarts the clean, simple lines of the lower body. From certain angles, the Zagato looks like a stubby El Camino pickup with an enclosed bed, but unlike an El Camino, it has another pair of seats behind the driver and the number­-one passenger. However, candidates for travel in back may want to suggest a democratic drawing of straws, fearing their upper and lower extremities will be forever molded into unnatural shapes. Lowering the back window pro­vides a modern version of the rumble seat and a bit more headroom, but no extra sympathy for the legs. The Zagato is not by any means or intent an appro­priate way to transport half your neigh­borhood to a formal dinner party. Con­sider it a sports car that happens to ben­efit from a slight extra people-carrying capacity suited to quick runs down to the beach, the movies, or the local wa­tering hole.

As always, Lancia has provided a nice setting for front-seat travelers, creating a modern environment that welcomes you with comfort—though the passen­ger is probably more comfortable than the driver. The seats are good, but the driver is squeezed into the classic Amer­ican-knees-in-the-American-armpits Italian driving position, arms stretching for a steering wheel that lies out near the horizon.

But inside the car, you tend to forget about the varied points of styling and sometimes even about the peculiar driv­ing position. Sometimes the Zagato is so much fun you can’t help yourself. Other people watch you rip past, and you know they’re thinking, “What would I do if I had that? What does it feel like without a roof or a back win­dow?” They figure anything with these looks must be kinda fast, and they won­der how many friends you can squeeze into the thing before the cops stop you. The Zagato is meant for the unpredict­able kind of fun you can have only if you’re unpredictable enough to have a car like this. If that’s eccentric, so be it.

raw_summary: Chinese-owned Polestar was banned from selling cars in the U.S. back in June, and like a scorned ex showing you what you're missing after a breakup, it's now revealed one of the coolest designs in recent memory: the Formula 2030 concept car. Look at what they took from us. It's got a low, wide, shooting brake shape. article_paragraphs: Chinese-owned Polestar was banned from selling cars in the U.S. back in June, and like a scorned ex showing you what you're missing after a breakup, it's now revealed one of the coolest designs in recent memory: the Formula 2030 concept car. Look at what they took from us.

It's got a low, wide, shooting brake shape. The big front door, little rear door setup is pure enthusiast bait, and the switchgear inside looks like it came straight off of professional audio equipment. The Formula 2030 isn't just a for-show concept car, either, because Polestar says it will indeed "point towards future design direction for the brand."

Specifically, "various design attributes" seen here will actually show up in the next-gen Polestar 2 and upcoming Polestar 7 compact SUV . The Formula 2030 is billed as a compact four-door sports car, not really fitting neatly into any existing segment. It sits lower than the Polestar 5 grand tourer , fits between the 2 compact sedan and 7 size-wise, and is probably closest to the Polestar 4 in spirit.

It already looks great at a glance, but things get way more interesting once you start opening stuff up. Both the hood and rear hatch open up clamshell-style, exposing the natural fiber composite chassis underneath and orange Öhlins dampers. The half-size rear doors are coach doors, giving the Formula no B-pillar and a huge opening when all doors are open.

Inside, a very curved instrument screen measuring 20 inches sits on top of the steering column while a 12.2-inch center touchscreen sits in the middle. That touchscreen can physically lower when the driver switches drive modes to Performance, and raise when the car is in Autonomous. Below this screen is an array of up to eight customizable rocker switches and knobs. You can swap the specific switches or knobs out, like you can with, say, a pro-grade video game controller, and their individual functions can also be configured to your liking. All four bucket seats sit low in the cabin and get inflatable bolsters and cushions for better support.

I've never really thought about how rare four-spoke wheels are, but looking at the 22s on this Polestar concept, I'm simultaneously sad that they aren't more common but also completely understand why that's the case. They're definitely weird, but I also sort of dig it?

It all adds up to a funky yet beautiful design that makes us hope Polestar will return to the U.S. market by the Formula 2030's namesake. Given the political conditions that led to its banning and how those tides are turning in this country , that scenario actually feels like a real possibility.

title: Juiced unveils another lower-cost moto-styled electric bike: Scrambler Core
raw_summary: Juiced Bikes is expanding its recently relaunched Scrambler lineup with a new, more affordable model known as the Juiced Scrambler Core . The new bike keeps much of the moto-inspired styling and performance of the existing Scrambler Hardtail, but trims back several components to knock several hundred dollars off the price.
